**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 33, verses 1–3**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ittaqi Allah* (﴿اتق الله﴾): Persist in His piety (taqwa) by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

*Wa la tuti al-kafirin* (﴿ولا تطع الكافرين﴾): The polytheists, in what they propose to you.

*Wal-munafiqin* (﴿والمنافقين﴾): Those who display faith and conceal disbelief, by threatening you with what they threaten you with.

*Inna Allaha kana alimhan hakima* (﴿إن الله كان عليما حكيما﴾): All-Knowing of His creation, outwardly and inwardly, and All-Wise in His management and His craftsmanship.

*Wattabi ma yuha ilayka min rabbika* (﴿واتبع ما يوحى إليك من ربك﴾): Adhere to what is legislated for you by your Lord, and do not turn your attention to what your adversaries say to you, whether proposals or threats.

*Wa tawakkal ala Allah* (﴿وتوكل على الله﴾): Entrust your affair to Him and proceed with what He has commanded you, unconcerned by anything.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The polytheists continued the proposals they had begun in Mecca and carried them on to Medina. These were offers of reconciliation between him and them, on condition that he abandon part of his religion or expel some of his companions. The hypocrites in Medina played their part by threatening him (ﷺ) with assassination by stealth if he did not cease mentioning the gods of the polytheists. It was at this particular juncture that God, the Exalted, revealed His words: ﴿O Prophet﴾. His Lord addressed him by the title of Prophethood, affirming it and honoring him, and did not address him by his personal name, as He addressed Musa (Moses), Isa (Jesus) and others by their names. He said: ﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ That is: fear God and be wary of Him. Do not accept the proposals of the polytheists, and do not be intimidated by the hypocrites' threat to kill you. Indeed God was and still is All-Knowing of all His creatures and of their actions, whether outward or inward, and All-Wise in His management and disposal of the affairs of His creatures and servants. By His knowledge and wisdom, He, the Exalted, will not forsake you or abandon you, and He will in no way allow your enemies or His enemies to reach you.

His words ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾ refer to the legislation, both particular and general. Do not leave any of it, small or great, for it is the path to your success and the ladder to your triumph. You and your community follow you in all of this.

His words ﴿Indeed God is well aware of what you do﴾ form a causal clause that carries both promise and warning. God's knowledge of the deeds of His servants, both good and corrupt, necessitates recompense for them. Whenever a deed is good, the recompense is good, and this contains His promise. Whenever a deed is corrupt, the recompense is evil, and this contains His warning.

His words ﴿And rely upon God; and God suffices as Guardian﴾ are a command from God, the Exalted, to His Messenger, whose community follows him, to place his trust in God regarding his affair, to proceed on his path implementing the rulings of his Lord, unconcerned by the disbelievers and the hypocrites. He also informed him, implicitly, that God will suffice him whenever he trusts in Him, and that God is sufficient as a Guardian and a protecting Trustee.

**Guidance from the verses (Hidayat al-Ayat, lessons drawn from the verses):**

1) The obligation to be mindful of God, the Exalted, by performing what He commands and abstaining from what He forbids.

2) The prohibition of obeying the disbelievers and the hypocrites in what they propose or threaten in order to bring it about.

3) The obligation to follow the Book and the Sunnah, to rely upon God, and to proceed in this without fear or trepidation.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 4–5:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾: that is, Allah did not create a man with two hearts, as some of the polytheists claimed.

﴿Those of you who divorce by zihar from their wives, [saying to them, "You are to me like the back of my mother"]...﴾: a man says to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother."

﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾: that is, He has not made the adopted child a son of the one who adopts him.

﴿That is merely your saying with your mouths﴾: that is, a mere utterance of the tongue with no reality outside it, so the wife does not become a mother, nor does the adopted child become a son.

﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah﴾: that is, more equitable.

﴿They are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾: that is, brothers in Islam and your paternal cousins. Whoever's father is not known, say to him: "O my brother" or "O my cousin."

﴿There is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred﴾: that is, there is no sin or wrongdoing in error. So whoever mistakenly says to an adopted child, "O son of so-and-so," he bears no sin.

﴿But what your hearts intend﴾: that is, sin and wrongdoing lie in deliberate intent, by attributing the adopted child to the one who adopted him.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾: therefore He does not hold you accountable for error, but only for deliberate intent.

Meaning of the verses:

Since the heart is the seat of reason and perception, the presence of two hearts in one man's body would produce a conflict leading to corruption in the life of the person with two hearts. Allah, exalted is He, did not make for a man two hearts within his body, as some people of Makkah claimed that Abu Ma'mar Jamil ibn Ma'mar al-Fihri had two hearts, because they witnessed his intelligence, eloquence and shrewdness, and this deceived them. He said, "I have two hearts with which I understand, better than the understanding of Muhammad (ﷺ)." So the verse was a refutation of him. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾. This contains an indication that one cannot combine love of Allah and love of His enemies, or obedience to Allah and obedience to His enemies.

His saying: ﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers﴾: that is, Allah did not make the wife, of whom a man made zihar, a mother to him who made zihar with her, such as saying to her, "You are to me like the back of my mother." The people of the Jahiliyyah considered zihar to make the wife forbidden like the mother. Allah nullified that and explained its ruling in Surah al-Mujadila: that whoever makes zihar with his wife must make expiation: freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty needy persons.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾: that is, Allah did not make the adopted child a son, although in the Jahiliyyah and in early Islam they called the adoptee a son, and full rights of sonship followed from that, such as the prohibition of marrying his wife if he divorced her or she was widowed. His saying: ﴿That is merely your saying with your mouths﴾: that is, it is nothing but speech from the mouth with no reality outside it, for a man's saying to the adopted child, "You are my son," does not make him his son, and a husband's saying to his wife, "You are like my mother," does not make her his mother. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah says the truth﴾, so the word "mother" is not applied to the one made zihar with, nor the word "son" to the adopted child. ﴿And He guides to the way﴾: that is, to the most upright and rightly guided path, glorified is He, there is no god but Him.

His saying, exalted is He, in verse [5] of this context: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾: that is, call the adopted children by their fathers, meaning attribute them to them, saying, "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so." For calling them by their fathers is more just and equitable in the judgment and legislation of Allah. ﴿And if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion﴾: so call them by the title of Islamic brotherhood, saying, "This is my brother in Islam." ﴿And your clients﴾: that is, your paternal cousins; call them by that, saying, "O son of my paternal uncle." If the adopted child is one whom you have freed, say to him, "My client." ﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾: that is, no sin or wrongdoing ﴿for that in which you have erred﴾: from one of you saying to the adopted child, "O son of so-and-so," addressing the one who adopted him, by mistake, a slip of the tongue without intention, or by supposing that he is his son while in reality he is not his son. But the sin lies in deliberate intent. His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾: that is, Forgiving to whoever repents, Merciful, not hastening punishment upon the one who disobeys, perhaps he will repent and return.

Guidance from the verses:

1) Nullification of the prohibition by zihar that existed in the Jahiliyyah.

2) Nullification of the custom of adoption and what follows from it, namely the prohibition of marrying the wife of the adopted son.

3) The obligation to call the adopted child by his father's name if it is known, even if he is a donkey.

4) If the adoptive father's son's father is not known, he is called by the title of Islamic brotherhood, or paternal cousinship, or clientage.

5) Lifting of blame and sin for error in general, and specifically in what the noble verse concerns, which is calling the adopted child by the name of the one who adopted him, a slip of the tongue without intention, or with intention because one considers him his son while he is not his son.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 6–8:

Explanation of the words:

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾: that is, concerning what he commands them and forbids them, and what he asks of them, he has more right to it than they have over themselves.

﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾: in terms of prohibition (marriage), whether the wives were divorced or widowed, may Allah be pleased with them.

﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another﴾: that is, in inheritance, among the emigrants and those bound by allegiance and alliance.

﴿Except that you do something kind for your allies﴾: by making a permissible bequest to them, which is one-third or less.

﴿That was written in the Book as inscribed﴾: that is, the non-inheritance through faith, emigration and alliance is written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾: that is, mention to your people that We took from the prophets their covenant that they would worship Allah alone and call to His worship.

﴿And from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses﴾: that is, We took it especially from you, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary; Muhammad ﷺ is mentioned first as an honour and exaltation of him.

﴿And We took from them a firm covenant﴾: that is, a strong one. The mithaq (covenant) is a binding pledge confirmed by oath.

﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾: that is, the covenant was taken so that the truthful, namely the prophets, would be questioned about their truthfulness in conveying the message, as a rebuke to the disbelievers who denied them.

﴿And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾: that is, He rewards the believers and has prepared for the disbelievers a painful, i.e. agonizing, punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah the Exalted nullified the custom of adoption, and the Prophet ﷺ had adopted Zayd ibn Harithah al-Kalbi, so that he was known as Zayd ibn Muhammad ﷺ, and then he came to be called Zayd ibn Harithah, mawla of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah the Exalted informed all believers that His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is closer to the believers than their own selves, and that his wives are their mothers in terms of prohibition, so the wife of the Prophet is not lawful to anyone after him ﷺ. The meaning of ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ is: concerning what he commands them, forbids them and asks of them, he has more right to it than they have over themselves. Through this Allah the Exalted gave His Messenger a elevation and exaltation of status that He did not give to anyone else, as a reward for his patience over what was taken from him concerning the sonship of Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him, who had been called Zayd ibn Muhammad and then came to be known as Zayd ibn Harithah.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another﴾ means in inheritance. By this verse Allah nullified inheritance through faith, emigration and the alliance that existed in early Islam, and inheritance became only through lineage, marriage and clientage (wala') and nothing else. His saying ﴿That was written in the Book as inscribed﴾ means that inheritance through blood relations, that is through kinship, is written in the Preserved Tablet. His saying ﴿Except that you do something kind for your allies﴾ means: except that you make a permissible bequest, which is one-third, to any of the believers, the emigrants, or those with whom you have made alliance; there is no harm in it, it is permissible and carries no prohibition.

His saying ﴿That was﴾ refers to what was mentioned of inheritance through kinship only, and the permissibility of bequeathing one-third to those whose inheritance through faith, emigration and brotherhood was nullified, ﴿in the Book﴾, which is the Preserved Tablet, the book of decrees, ﴿inscribed﴾, meaning written and recorded, so it is not lawful to alter or change it.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾ means: mention, O Our Messenger, to your people that We took the covenant, which is a binding pledge confirmed by oath, from the prophets in general, that they would worship Allah alone and call their nations to that; and from the resolute messengers (ulu al-'azm) in particular, who are you, O Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary. His saying ﴿And We took from them a firm covenant﴾ repeats the wording to affirm it, and so that his saying ﴿That He may question﴾ may be consequent upon it, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the truthful﴾, who are the prophets, ﴿about their truthfulness﴾ in conveying their message, as a rebuke to their nations who disbelieved and denied them. He rewarded the believers, ﴿and He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾, meaning agonizing, which is the punishment of the Fire.

Guidance from the verses:

1) The obligation to give precedence to what the Messenger wants from the believer over what the believer wants for himself.

2) The prohibition on marrying the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, who are the Mothers of the Believers, and he ﷺ is like a father to them.

3) The nullification of inheritance through brotherhood (mu'akhah), emigration and alliance that existed in early Islam.

4) The permissibility of bequeathing to a non-heir up to one-third or less.

5) The obligation to affirm the oneness of Allah the Exalted in worship and to call people to it.

6) The affirmation of Tawhid by taking the covenant concerning it from all the prophets and messengers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verse 9–14:

Explanation of the words:

"Remember the favour of Allah upon you": i.e., remember the favour of Allah, that is, His defending you, so that you may be thankful for that.

"Hosts": i.e., the hosts of the polytheists who formed factions.

"Winds and hosts you did not see": these were the hosts of the angels, and the wind was the ṣabā (the east wind), which blows from the east.

"And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do": i.e., Seeing of your deeds, such as digging the trench and the preparations for battle.

"When they came upon you from above you": i.e., the Banu Asad and Ghaṭafān came from the direction of Najd, from the east of Madinah.

"And from below you": i.e., from the west, and they were Quraysh and Kinanah.

"And when the eyes shifted": i.e., they turned away from everything except the enemy, which they looked at out of intense terror.

"And the hearts reached the throats": i.e., reached the extremity of the windpipe from intense fear.

"And you were thinking about Allah different thoughts": i.e., varied thoughts of victory and defeat, and of salvation and destruction.

"There the believers were tested": i.e., then, in the trench and on the battlefield, the believers were tried.

"And they were shaken with a severe shaking": i.e., they were moved with a strong agitation from intense terror.

"And those in whose hearts is disease": i.e., some measure of hypocrisy, because of the weakness of their faith.

"Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion": i.e., what we were promised of victory was nothing but delusion and falsehood.

"O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you": i.e., O people of Madinah, there is no station for you around the trench, so return to your homes.

"Indeed, our houses are exposed": i.e., not secure.

"They intend only to flee": i.e., from the fighting, since their houses are secure.

"Had it been entered upon them": i.e., Madinah, meaning the invading enemy had entered it.

"Then they were asked for fitnah": i.e., then they were asked to revert to polytheism, and they would have given it, i.e., granted it and done it.

"And they would not have hesitated therein except briefly": i.e., they would not have delayed or paused, but would have hastened to respond and apostatized.

Explanation of the verses:

The Most High said, "O you who have believed, remember the favour of Allah upon you when there came to you hosts," and these verses recount the story of the Battle of the Trench, or the Confederates. The Blessed and Most High related it to the believers in the context of reminding them of His favours upon them, so that they would be thankful by submission and obedience to Allah and His Messenger and by accepting everything prescribed for them, for their perfection and happiness in both lives. So He said, "O you who have believed," i.e., O you who have believed in Allah as Lord and God, in Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and in Islam as religion and law. "Remember the favour of Allah upon you," represented in the averting of the greatest danger that had befallen you, namely the gathering of many armies to attack you in the heart of your homes: the armies of Quraysh, Asad, Ghaṭafān, and the Banu Qurayẓah of the Jews. Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab al-Naḍarī incited them against you and united their factions, seeking revenge on the Messenger and the believers, since they had expelled them from Madinah and driven them out, so they joined the Jews of Khaybar and Taymā'. When the Prophet ﷺ received news of them, he ordered the digging of a trench beneath the slope of Mount Sal‘ to the west of Madinah, on the suggestion of Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him), who had military experience learned from the lands of his people, Persia.

The digging of the trench was completed within the span of a month. The Prophet ﷺ assigned to every ten men forty cubits, that is, twenty meters. As soon as they finished digging it, the armies of the polytheists arrived, numbering about twelve thousand. When they saw the Messenger and the Muslims behind the trench beneath Mount Sal‘, they said, "This is a stratagem the Arabs did not know." They skirmished with arrows, and ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wadd al-Qurashi drove his horse into the trench and ‘Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) killed him. The siege and skirmishing continued, and the days and nights were cold, and famine pitched its tents for about a month.

The details of the story, as Allah mentioned them, are as follows:

As for His saying, "When there came to you hosts," these were the hosts of the polytheists from Quraysh and from Banu Asad and Ghaṭafān. "Then We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see": when the hosts of the polytheists came to you and besieged you at the slope of Sal‘, We sent upon them a wind, the blessed ṣabā, about which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was helped by the ṣabā, and ‘Ād was destroyed by the dabūr," and the dabūr is the western wind. The ṣabā did such deeds to them that it left them no fire without extinguishing it, no cooking pot on its stones without overturning it, and no tent or pavilion without knocking it down and removing it, until they were compelled to depart. As for His saying, "and hosts you did not see," these were the angels, who struck them with terror and fear, which deprived them of all their judgment and sound sense, and they returned dragging the trails of disappointment. Praise be to Allah. As for His saying, "And ever is Allah of what you do, Seeing": i.e., of all your deeds, such as digging the trench, the struggles and maneuvers, and what the hypocrites said and did; nothing of it was hidden from Him, and He will recompense the good-doer with good and the wrongdoer with wrong.

As for His saying, "When they came to you from above you," i.e., the polytheists, "from above you," i.e., from the east, and they were Ghaṭafān under the leadership of ‘Uyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn, and Asad; "and from below you," and they were Quraysh and Kinanah, i.e., from the southwest, and this is a specification of the battlefield. As for His saying, "And when the eyes shifted," i.e., they turned away from everything, so that they looked at nothing except the invading forces, out of intense fear. "And the hearts reached the throats": i.e., they rose with the rising of the lungs until they reached the extremity of the windpipe. As for His saying, "And you were thinking about Allah different thoughts": varied thoughts of victory and defeat, safety and perishing, and this is a depiction of the situation of the most eloquent kind, and it is, as the Most High mentioned, literally so.

As for His saying, "There" i.e., in that place and at that time when the enemy surrounded you, "the believers were tested": i.e., their Lord tested them to see who would remain steadfast in his faith, whom hardships and trials could not shake, and who would quickly flee and turn away because of weakness of faith, little resolve and little patience. As for His saying, "and they were shaken with a severe shaking": i.e., they were disturbed and moved with a strong agitation, because of the strength of the enemy and the abundance of its hosts, the weakness of the believers and their small number, the factor of famine and siege, the severe cold, the cowardice displayed by the hypocrites, and what the situation revealed of the breach of their covenant by the Banu Qurayẓah and their joining of the confederates.

As for His saying, "And when the hypocrites said, and those in whose hearts is disease": i.e., hypocrisy, because of the weakness of their faith. "Allah and His Messenger promised us": i.e., of victory, "nothing but delusion": i.e., falsehood. That was because, when they were digging in the trench, a rock resisted them and refused to break, so the Prophet ﷺ was called to it, and he struck it with the pickaxe, a blow that split it and from which a flash of light came forth that illuminated the whole area, so the Prophet ﷺ said "Allahu akbar" and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." Then he struck it a second time, splitting it, and a flash came from it that lit up what lay between the two lava plains of Madinah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said "Allahu akbar," a takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." He struck a third time and broke it, and a flash came from it like the previous two, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said "Allahu akbar" and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took Salman by the hand and ascended from the trench. Salman said, "My father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, I have seen something I had never seen before." The Messenger of Allah turned to the people and said, "Did you see what Salman saw?" They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He informed them that by the light of that flash he had seen the palaces of the cities of Kisra like the fangs of dogs, and that Jibril had informed him that my community would prevail over them. As he saw in the second strike the red palaces of the land of Rome, and Jibril informed him that my community would prevail over them, and he saw in the third the palaces of Ṣan‘ā', and Jibril informed him that my community would prevail over them. So rejoice, rejoice, rejoice. The Muslims rejoiced and said, "Praise be to Allah, a promise of truth."

When the siege was prolonged, the hardship intensified, and fear gained control over the men, the hypocrites and those weak in faith said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion," for Mu‘attib ibn Qushayr said, "Muhammad promises us the conquest of Persia and Rome, while one of us cannot even relieve himself for fear. This is nothing but a promise of delusion!!"

As for His saying, "And when a group of them said": i.e., of the hypocrites, and he was Aws ibn Qayẓī, one of the leaders of the hypocrites, "O people of Yathrib," i.e., of Madinah, before the Messenger abolished this name for it and called it Madinah, "there is no station for you": i.e., at the slope of Sal‘ by the trench, "so return" to your dwellings inside Madinah, on the pretext that there is no benefit in remaining here without fighting. He said this only to flee from fighting and escape confrontation. As for His saying, "And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet," i.e., they asked permission to return to their homes in Madinah, claiming that their houses were exposed, i.e., open to the enemy, and they felt insecure about them. Allah refuted their claim, saying, "And they were not exposed; they intended only to flee," i.e., by this excuse they only intended to flee from the face of the enemy. The Most High said about them, "And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?" "Had it been entered upon them," i.e., Madinah, "from its surrounding areas," i.e., from all its sides, east, west, north and south, "then they were asked for fitnah," i.e., then the invading enemy who entered Madinah asked them to apostatize, that is, to return to polytheism, "they would have given it," i.e., granted it immediately, "and they would not have hesitated therein except briefly," until they apostatized from Islam and became as they had been, polytheists, and Allah forbid, from hypocrisy and the hypocrites.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1) The legitimacy of reminding people of blessings so that those reminded may be thankful for them, and their obedience to Allah and His Messenger may increase.

2) The presentation of the Battle of the Confederates or the Trench as a truthful account, unsurpassed in presenting events for the sake of lesson.

3) The clarification that the Battle of the Trench was among the most severe and most painful and exhausting battles for the Muslims.

4) The clarification that good opinion of Allah is praiseworthy, and that bad opinion of Him, the Most High, is disbelief and hypocrisy.

5) The clarification of the positions of the hypocrites calling to defeat, so that this may be a lesson for the believers.

6) The affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood through reports of the unseen which the Messenger of Allah gave, and which came to pass as he said, regarding the conquest of Persia, Rome and Yemen.

The Blessed and Most High related it to the believers in the context of reminding them of His favours upon them, so that they would be thankful by submission and obedience to Allah and His Messenger and by accepting everything prescribed for them, for their perfection and happiness in both lives. So He said, "O you who have believed," i.e., O you who have believed in Allah as Lord and God, in Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and in Islam as religion and law. "Remember the favour of Allah upon you," represented in the averting of the greatest danger that had befallen you, namely the gathering of many armies to attack you in the heart of your homes: the armies of Quraysh, Asad, Ghaṭafān, and the Banu Qurayẓah of the Jews. Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab al-Naḍarī incited them against you and united their factions, seeking revenge on the Messenger and the believers, since they had expelled them from Madinah and driven them out, so they joined the Jews of Khaybar and Taymā'. When the Prophet ﷺ received news of them, he ordered the digging of a trench beneath the slope of Mount Sal‘ to the west of Madinah, on the suggestion of Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him), who had military experience learned from the lands of his people, Persia.

The digging of the trench was completed within the span of a month. The Prophet ﷺ assigned to every ten men forty cubits, that is, twenty meters. As soon as they finished digging it, the armies of the polytheists arrived, numbering about twelve thousand. When they saw the Messenger and the Muslims behind the trench beneath Mount Sal‘, they said, "This is a stratagem the Arabs did not know." They skirmished with arrows, and ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wadd al-Qurashi drove his horse into the trench and ‘Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) killed him. The siege and skirmishing continued, and the days and nights were cold, and famine pitched its tents for about a month.

The details of the story, as Allah mentioned them, are as follows:

As for His saying, "When there came to you hosts," these were the hosts of the polytheists from Quraysh and from Banu Asad and Ghaṭafān. "Then We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see": when the hosts of the polytheists came to you and besieged you at the slope of Sal‘, We sent upon them a wind, the blessed ṣabā, about which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was helped by the ṣabā, and ‘Ād was destroyed by the dabūr," and the dabūr is the western wind. The ṣabā did such deeds to them that it left them no fire without extinguishing it, no cooking pot on its stones without overturning it, and no tent or pavilion without knocking it down and removing it, until they were compelled to depart. As for His saying, "and hosts you did not see," these were the angels, who struck them with terror and fear, which deprived them of all their judgment and sound sense, and they returned dragging the trails of disappointment. Praise be to Allah. As for His saying, "And ever is Allah of what you do, Seeing": i.e., of all your deeds, such as digging the trench, the struggles and maneuvers, and what the hypocrites said and did; nothing of it was hidden from Him, and He will recompense the good-doer with good and the wrongdoer with wrong.

As for His saying, "When they came to you from above you," i.e., the polytheists, "from above you," i.e., from the east, and they were Ghaṭafān under the leadership of ‘Uyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn, and Asad; "and from below you," and they were Quraysh and Kinanah, i.e., from the southwest, and this is a specification of the battlefield. As for His saying, "And when the eyes shifted," i.e., they turned away from everything, so that they looked at nothing except the invading forces, out of intense fear. "And the hearts reached the throats": i.e., they rose with the rising of the lungs until they reached the extremity of the windpipe. As for His saying, "And you were thinking about Allah different thoughts": varied thoughts of victory and defeat, safety and perishing, and this is a depiction of the situation of the most eloquent kind, and it is, as the Most High mentioned, literally so.

As for His saying, "There" i.e., in that place and at that time when the enemy surrounded you, "the believers were tested": i.e., their Lord tested them to see who would remain steadfast in his faith, whom hardships and trials could not shake, and who would quickly flee and turn away because of weakness of faith, little resolve and little patience. As for His saying, "and they were shaken with a severe shaking": i.e., they were disturbed and moved with a strong agitation, because of the strength of the enemy and the abundance of its hosts, the weakness of the believers and their small number, the factor of famine and siege, the severe cold, the cowardice displayed by the hypocrites, and what the situation revealed of the breach of their covenant by the Banu Qurayẓah and their joining of the confederates.

As for His saying, "And when the hypocrites said, and those in whose hearts is disease": i.e., hypocrisy, because of the weakness of their faith. "Allah and His Messenger promised us": i.e., of victory, "nothing but delusion": i.e., falsehood. That was because, when they were digging in the trench, a rock resisted them and refused to break, so the Prophet ﷺ was called to it, and he struck it with the pickaxe, a blow that split it and from which a flash of light came forth that illuminated the whole area, so the Prophet ﷺ said "Allahu akbar" and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." Then he struck it a second time, splitting it, and a flash came from it that lit up what lay between the two lava plains of Madinah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said "Allahu akbar," a takbir of conquest, and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." He struck a third time and broke it, and a flash came from it like the previous two, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said "Allahu akbar" and the Muslims said "Allahu akbar." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took Salman by the hand and ascended from the trench. Salman said, "My father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, I have seen something I had never seen before." The Messenger of Allah turned to the people and said, "Did you see what Salman saw?" They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He informed them that by the light of that flash he had seen the palaces of the cities of Kisra like the fangs of dogs, and that Jibril had informed him that my community would prevail over them. As he saw in the second strike the red palaces of the land of Rome, and Jibril informed him that my community would prevail over them, and he saw in the third the palaces of Ṣan‘ā', and Jibril informed him that my community would prevail over them. So rejoice, rejoice, rejoice. The Muslims rejoiced and said, "Praise be to Allah, a promise of truth."

When the siege was prolonged, the hardship intensified, and fear gained control over the men, the hypocrites and those weak in faith said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion," for Mu‘attib ibn Qushayr said, "Muhammad promises us the conquest of Persia and Rome, while one of us cannot even relieve himself for fear. This is nothing but a promise of delusion!!"

As for His saying, "And when a group of them said": i.e., of the hypocrites, and he was Aws ibn Qayẓī, one of the leaders of the hypocrites, "O people of Yathrib," i.e., of Madinah, before the Messenger abolished this name for it and called it Madinah, "there is no station for you": i.e., at the slope of Sal‘ by the trench, "so return" to your dwellings inside Madinah, on the pretext that there is no benefit in remaining here without fighting. He said this only to flee from fighting and escape confrontation. As for His saying, "And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet," i.e., they asked permission to return to their homes in Madinah, claiming that their houses were exposed, i.e., open to the enemy, and they felt insecure about them. Allah refuted their claim, saying, "And they were not exposed; they intended only to flee," i.e., by this excuse they only intended to flee from the face of the enemy. The Most High said about them, "And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?" "Had it been entered upon them," i.e., Madinah, "from its surrounding areas," i.e., from all its sides, east, west, north and south, "then they were asked for fitnah," i.e., then the invading enemy who entered Madinah asked them to apostatize, that is, to return to polytheism, "they would have given it," i.e., granted it immediately, "and they would not have hesitated therein except briefly," until they apostatized from Islam and became as they had been, polytheists, and Allah forbid, from hypocrisy and the hypocrites.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1) The legitimacy of reminding people of blessings so that those reminded may be thankful for them, and their obedience to Allah and His Messenger may increase.

2) The presentation of the Battle of the Confederates or the Trench as a truthful account, unsurpassed in presenting events for the sake of lesson.

3) The clarification that the Battle of the Trench was among the most severe and most painful and exhausting battles for the Muslims.

4) The clarification that good opinion of Allah is praiseworthy, and that bad opinion of Him, the Most High, is disbelief and hypocrisy.

5) The clarification of the positions of the hypocrites calling to defeat, so that this may be a lesson for the believers.

6) The affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood through reports of the unseen which the Messenger of Allah gave, and which came to pass as he said, regarding the conquest of Persia, Rome and Yemen.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 15–19:

Explanation of the words:

﻿"And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, [that] they would not turn their backs": i.e., before the Battle of the Trench, and that was on the day of Uhud. They said: "By Allah, if Allah makes us witness fighting, we will surely fight and not turn our backs."

"And the covenant of Allah will be questioned": i.e., the one who made the covenant will be held accountable for fulfilling it.

"And then you would not enjoy [life] except for a little": i.e., if you flee from fighting, you will not enjoy life except for a little, and then you will die.

"Who is it that can protect you from Allah?": i.e., who can grant you protection and safeguard you from Allah.

"If He intends for you harm": i.e., a punishment that will distress and grieve you.

"Allah already knows those among you who hinder": i.e., those who discourage from fighting and who dissuade their brothers from it, so that they do not fight alongside the Messenger of Allah and the believers.

"Come to us": i.e., come to us, and do not go out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

"And they do not come to battle except a little": i.e., and they do not witness the fighting except a little, to ward off from themselves the accusation of hypocrisy.

"Stingy toward you": i.e., miserly, not spending on your good causes, such as the expenses of jihad, or on the poor.

"Their eyes roll like one overcome by death": i.e., their eyes roll from intense fear because of their cowardice, like the dying person who swoons, i.e., faints from the pains of the agony of death.

"They will assail you with sharp tongues": i.e., they will harm you with sharp, cutting tongues like iron, by means of their excessive talk and boasting in words without deeds.

"Stingy in regard to the good": i.e., miserly with good; they do not give it, nor do they do it, nor even say it.

"Those have not believed": i.e., they have not believed with true faith, therefore they are cowardly at the encounter and stingy at the giving.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to present the events of the Battle of the Confederates. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they had already made a covenant with Allah before﴾, i.e., those hypocrites had already made a covenant with Allah before the Battle of the Confederates, and that was on the day they fled from the Battle of Uhud, which was about two years before the Battle of the Confederates. They said, "By Allah, if Allah makes us witness fighting, we will surely fight and not turn our backs." So Allah reminded them of their covenant that they had bound upon themselves, and then they broke it. ﴿And the covenant of Allah will be questioned﴾, i.e., its party will be asked about it and held accountable for it. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing"﴾, i.e., say to them, O our Messenger, that flight will not benefit you, that is, fleeing from death or killing, because the appointed terms are fixed, and whoever does not die by the sword dies by other means; so there is no sense in fleeing from fighting when it is obligatory. And His saying, ﴿And then you would not enjoy [life] except for a little﴾, i.e., if you flee from fighting, you will not enjoy life except for a little time, and then you will die at the end of your lifespans, which is a brief period. So fleeing does not lengthen your lives, and fighting does not shorten them. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?"﴾, i.e., say to them, O our Messenger, as a rebuke, reproach, and also instruction: who is it that can protect you, i.e., grant you protection and safeguard you, from Allah? ﴿If He intends for you harm﴾, i.e., what would displease you of affliction, killing, or the like, ﴿or intends for you mercy﴾, i.e., safety and good. There is no one who can prevent that from reaching you, because Allah grants protection and no one can grant protection against Him. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or any helper﴾, i.e., those who oppose the command of Allah and disobey Him and His Messenger will not find, besides Allah, a protector to take them under his care and repel from them what Allah intends for them of evil, nor a helper to aid them when Allah intends to humiliate and forsake them because of their evil deeds. And His saying in verse [18] in this context: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder﴾, Allah, exalted is He, informs them that He has already known those who hinder, i.e., who discourage from fighting and who undermine by what they say secretly among the ranks of the believers, like the fifth column in wars: people who mention in private the greatness and strength of the enemy, fearing it and discouraging others from fighting it.

And His saying: ﴿And those who say to their brothers, "Come to us"﴾, i.e., come to us, to Medina, and leave Muhammad and his companions to die alone, for they are no more than a mouthful of a camel. And His saying: ﴿And they do not come to battle except a little﴾, i.e., those hypocrites who discourage and those who said, "Indeed our houses are exposed," do not witness or attend the fighting except a little. They lag behind in most of the expeditions, and if they attend a battle once, they do so only to ward off the reproach of lagging behind and to repel the accusation of hypocrisy that has clung to them.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Stingy toward you﴾: He described them with miserliness after describing them with cowardice, and these two are the worst qualities of a person, i.e., cowardice and miserliness; stingy toward you, i.e., miserly, spending neither with you on jihad nor on the poor and needy. And His saying: ﴿So when fear comes﴾, i.e., because of the enemy's attack, ﴿you see them﴾, O Messenger, ﴿looking at you﴾ seeking refuge in you, ﴿their eyes rolling﴾ from fear, ﴿like one overcome by death﴾, who is dying and swoons because of what he suffers from the agonies of death. This is a striking depiction of the extent of the cowardice and fear that the hypocrites have, and the cause of this is disbelief and lack of faith in destiny, resurrection, and recompense.

And His saying: ﴿But when fear has departed﴾, i.e., its causes have ceased with the end of the war, ﴿they will assail you with sharp tongues﴾, i.e., those cowards at the encounter will assail you, striking you with sharp, cutting tongues like iron, by demanding the spoils or by false boasting that they did this and that. This has been their condition until today.

And His saying: ﴿Stingy toward the good﴾, i.e., miserly toward projects of good and what is spent in the way of Allah; they do not spend, because they do not believe in replacement, reward, or recompense, due to their disbelief in Allah and in meeting Him. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those have not believed﴾, so He recorded upon them the description of disbelief and set its consequences upon it, saying: ﴿So Allah has rendered their deeds void﴾, i.e., nullified them, so they will not be rewarded for them, because they are the deeds of a polytheist, and the deeds of a polytheist are void. And His saying: ﴿And that is ever, for Allah, easy﴾, i.e., nullifying their deeds and frustrating them in them and depriving them of their reward is easy for Allah, not difficult. Thus it has occurred as Allah, exalted is He, informed.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1) The obligation to fulfill covenants, since breaking a covenant is a sign of hypocrisy.

2) Abandoning jihad out of fear of being killed is an unrighteous act, since fighting does not shorten a lifespan and abandoning it does not lengthen it.

3) Stinginess and cowardice are among the qualities of the hypocrites, and they are the worst qualities in a human being.

4) Chattering, excessive talk, and boasting with words are qualities of people of cowardice and hypocrisy.

5) Disbelief nullifies deeds.

And His saying: ﴿And that is ever, for Allah, easy﴾, i.e., nullifying their deeds and frustrating them in them and depriving them of their reward is easy for Allah, not difficult. Thus it has occurred as Allah, exalted is He, informed.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1) The obligation to fulfill covenants, since breaking a covenant is a sign of hypocrisy.

2) Abandoning jihad out of fear of being killed is an unrighteous act, since fighting does not shorten a lifespan and abandoning it does not lengthen it.

3) Stinginess and cowardice are among the qualities of the hypocrites, and they are the worst qualities in a human being.

4) Chattering, excessive talk, and boasting with words are qualities of people of cowardice and hypocrisy.

5) Disbelief nullifies deeds.

Wa-sadaqa Allah wa-rasuluh (and Allah and His Messenger spoke truly): regarding the promise He made.

Wa-ma zadahum illa iman wa-taslima (and it only increased them in faith and submission): that is, affirmation of Allah's promise and submission to Allah's command.

Sadaqu ma 'ahadu Allah 'alayh (they were true to what they covenanted with Allah): that is, they fulfilled their pledge.

Faminhum man qada nahbahu (among them is one who has fulfilled his vow): that is, he fulfilled his pledge by fighting until he was martyred.

The context still continues to narrate the events of the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwat al-Ahzab). This is the utmost of cowardice and fear. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And if the confederates should come﴾, means: again, supposing and assuming it, ﴿they would wish on that day﴾ ﴿that they were in the desert with the Bedouins﴾, that is, outside Medina among the Bedouin nomads, out of their great fear of the attacking confederates. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿They would ask about your news﴾, means: about your reports, whether the confederates had prevailed over you or not. ﴿And if they were among you﴾, that is, present among you and not in the desert, ﴿they would not fight except a little﴾. This is due to their cowardice and their lack of faith in the benefit of fighting, because of their disbelief in meeting Allah and in what He has of reward and punishment. This is what the first verse [20] contains.

As for His saying in the second verse [21]: ﴿Indeed there has been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often﴾. His saying ﴿and it only increased them﴾, that is, their seeing the confederates despite their great numbers, ﴿in faith﴾ in the truthful promise of Allah, ﴿and submission﴾ to His decree and judgment. This is a fragrant praise from their Lord, mighty and majestic, for the sincere believers.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Among the believers are men who were true to what they covenanted with Allah﴾: this is another praise for some of the believers who had stayed behind from Badr and grieved over it, and when they suffered defeat at Uhud, they covenanted with Allah that if He let them witness fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would certainly fight until martyrdom. Allah, exalted is He, informs about them with His saying, ﴿Of them is one who has fulfilled his vow﴾, that is, he fulfilled his pledge by fighting until he was martyred, ﴿and of them is one who awaits﴾ death in the way of Allah. His saying ﴿that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾ means: Allah, exalted is He, caused those events to occur as He had decreed them in the Book of Destinies, so that He might reward the truthful for their truthfulness, honouring them and bestowing blessings upon them in His presence, and punish the hypocrites with His fire if He wills, by causing them to die before repenting, or He turns to them in forgiveness so that they believe, affirm His oneness, and enter Paradise along with the sincere believers. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and punish the hypocrites if He wills﴾ this for them by decree and destiny, or He turns to them in forgiveness so that they repent and are not punished. His saying, exalted is He, at the end of this context [25]: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved﴾, namely Quraysh, Kinana, Asad and Ghatafan, repelled them in their rage, that is, in their distress and grief, since they did not gain the Messenger and the believers and did not achieve anything of what they had hoped to achieve. ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, since He sent upon the confederates the wind and the angels, so they were routed and fled back to their homes, gaining nothing good. ﴿And Allah is ever Powerful, Exalted in Might﴾, that is, capable of bringing into being whatever He wills to bring into being, overpowering His affair, so that nothing He wills is prevented.

Lessons from the verses:

1) Affirmation that disbelief and hypocrisy bring with them cowardice, weakness, stinginess and miserliness, which never leave their possessor.

2) The obligation to follow the Messenger of Allah in everything the Muslim servant is able to do and is capable of.

3) Allah's praise of the sincere believers for their honourable stances and their fulfilment of their covenants.

4) Censure of the defeatists, the cowardly hypocrites and the weak in faith who break their covenants.

5) Explanation of the wisdom in the Battle of the Confederates: "that Allah may reward the truthful..." etc.

This is the utmost of cowardice and fear. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And if the confederates should come﴾, means: again, supposing and assuming it, ﴿they would wish on that day﴾ ﴿that they were in the desert with the Bedouins﴾, that is, outside Medina among the Bedouin nomads, out of their great fear of the attacking confederates. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿They would ask about your news﴾, means: about your reports, whether the confederates had prevailed over you or not. ﴿And if they were among you﴾, that is, present among you and not in the desert, ﴿they would not fight except a little﴾. This is due to their cowardice and their lack of faith in the benefit of fighting, because of their disbelief in meeting Allah and in what He has of reward and punishment. This is what the first verse [20] contains.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 26–27:

Explanation of the words:

ظاهروهم (zaharuhum): i.e., they supported them and stood behind them, strengthening their resolve.

من صياصيهم (min sayasihim): i.e., from their fortresses. Al-sayasi is the plural of sayasiyyah (a fortified place), meaning anything one takes refuge in.

وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب (wa-qadhafa fi qulubihim al-ru'b): i.e., He cast fear into their souls, so they became afraid.

وأرضاً لم تطأوها (wa-ardan lam tatauha): i.e., land you had not yet trodden. It is Khaybar, which was conquered after the Battle of the Trench (ghazwat al-khandaq).

The meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them﴾. This begins the account of the Battle of Banu Qurayza, which took place shortly after the Battle of the Trench, in the fifth year after the Hijra, at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah. The summary of this event is that when the confederates (al-ahzab) withdrew and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers returned to Madinah, Banu Qurayza had broken their covenant and joined the polytheist confederates, aiding them against the Messenger of Allah and the believers. When the confederates departed and the Messenger and the believers withdrew from the trench to Madinah, the people were startled only by the herald of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ calling out: "None of you should pray the 'asr except at Banu Qurayza," and Banu Qurayza were several miles from Madinah. This was because Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ that day at midday and said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you laid down your weapons? Allah commands you to march to Banu Qurayza." So the Messenger of Allah stood up and ordered a herald to call out the departure to Banu Qurayza. The Messenger of Allah and the Muslims went and besieged them for about twenty-five nights, and the siege distressed them, and Allah cast fear into their hearts. The Messenger of Allah said to them: "Will you submit to my judgment?" They refused. He said: "Will you submit to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh?" They said: "Yes," and so he judged concerning them, ruling that the men be killed, the children and women be taken captive, and the property be divided. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, confirming the ruling, said: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then confined them in the house of the daughter of al-Harith from the women of Banu al-Najjar, and went out to the market of Madinah and dug trenches there. Then they were brought forth, among them Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who had incited the confederates, and Ka'b ibn Asad, chief of Banu Qurayza. He ordered 'Ali and al-Zubayr to strike off their necks and throw them into that trench.

With this, the hostile Jewish presence in the Prophetic city came to an end. All praise is due to Allah.

As for His saying, ﴿And He brought down﴾, i.e., Allah, by His power, ﴿those of the People of the Book who supported them﴾, i.e., who backed the confederates and aided them against the Messenger and the believers, namely the Jews of Banu Qurayza. ﴿From their fortresses﴾, i.e., He brought them down from their strongholds in which they had taken refuge. ﴿And He cast fear into their hearts﴾, and for this reason they accepted arbitration. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed as judge over them the chief of the Aws, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, who ruled that the fighting men be killed and the women and children be taken captive. This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿a group you kill﴾, namely the men, ﴿and a group you take captive﴾, namely the women and children. And His saying, ﴿and He caused you to inherit their land﴾, the cultivated land, ﴿and their homes﴾, the dwellings, ﴿and their wealth﴾, both the silent and the speaking [i.e., goods and livestock]. And His saying, ﴿and land you had not trodden﴾, i.e., He made you inherit land you had not yet trodden, which is the land of Khaybar, where the Messenger of Allah campaigned against them in the sixth year after the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, and Allah granted them its conquest. And His saying, ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, is a concluding statement intended to affirm what Allah, may He be exalted, reported concerning the victory of His allies and the defeat of His enemies.

Guidance from the verses:

1) The demonstration of the consequence of treachery: when Qurayza betrayed the Messenger of Allah, He took vengeance upon them, empowering His Messenger and the believers against them, and they wiped them out entirely, leaving none but those who bore no guilt, namely the women and children.

2) The demonstration of the truthfulness of Allah's promise, for He caused the Muslims to inherit land they had not trodden: Khaybar, Syria, Iraq, Persia, and other great and numerous lands.

3) The affirmation that Allah's power is never limited; He, may He be exalted, is over all things competent, and nothing can overpower Him.

When the confederates departed and the Messenger and the believers withdrew from the trench to Madinah, the people were startled only by the herald of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ calling out: "None of you should pray the 'asr except at Banu Qurayza," and Banu Qurayza were several miles from Madinah. This was because Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ that day at midday and said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you laid down your weapons? Allah commands you to march to Banu Qurayza." So the Messenger of Allah stood up and ordered a herald to call out the departure to Banu Qurayza. The Messenger of Allah and the Muslims went and besieged them for about twenty-five nights, and the siege distressed them, and Allah cast fear into their hearts. The Messenger of Allah said to them: "Will you submit to my judgment?" They refused. He said: "Will you submit to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh?" They said: "Yes," and so he judged concerning them, ruling that the men be killed, the children and women be taken captive, and the property be divided. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, confirming the ruling, said: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then confined them in the house of the daughter of al-Harith from the women of Banu al-Najjar, and went out to the market of Madinah and dug trenches there. Then they were brought forth, among them Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who had incited the confederates, and Ka'b ibn Asad, chief of Banu Qurayza. He ordered 'Ali and al-Zubayr to strike off their necks and throw them into that trench.

With this, the hostile Jewish presence in the Prophetic city came to an end. All praise is due to Allah.

As for His saying, ﴿And He brought down﴾, i.e., Allah, by His power, ﴿those of the People of the Book who supported them﴾, i.e., who backed the confederates and aided them against the Messenger and the believers, namely the Jews of Banu Qurayza. ﴿From their fortresses﴾, i.e., He brought them down from their strongholds in which they had taken refuge. ﴿And He cast fear into their hearts﴾, and for this reason they accepted arbitration. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed as judge over them the chief of the Aws, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, who ruled that the fighting men be killed and the women and children be taken captive. This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿a group you kill﴾, namely the men, ﴿and a group you take captive﴾, namely the women and children. And His saying, ﴿and He caused you to inherit their land﴾, the cultivated land, ﴿and their homes﴾, the dwellings, ﴿and their wealth﴾, both the silent and the speaking [i.e., goods and livestock]. And His saying, ﴿and land you had not trodden﴾, i.e., He made you inherit land you had not yet trodden, which is the land of Khaybar, where the Messenger of Allah campaigned against them in the sixth year after the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, and Allah granted them its conquest. And His saying, ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, is a concluding statement intended to affirm what Allah, may He be exalted, reported concerning the victory of His allies and the defeat of His enemies.

Guidance from the verses:

1) The demonstration of the consequence of treachery: when Qurayza betrayed the Messenger of Allah, He took vengeance upon them, empowering His Messenger and the believers against them, and they wiped them out entirely, leaving none but those who bore no guilt, namely the women and children.

2) The demonstration of the truthfulness of Allah's promise, for He caused the Muslims to inherit land they had not trodden: Khaybar, Syria, Iraq, Persia, and other great and numerous lands.

3) The affirmation that Allah's power is never limited; He, may He be exalted, is over all things competent, and nothing can overpower Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 28–30:

Explanation of the words:

"Qul li-azwajika" (Say to your wives): i.e., those who were under his care at that time, nine in number, who asked him for an increase in maintenance (nafaqah) for themselves, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not have what would allow him to give them more.

"Fa-ta'alayna" (Then come): i.e., to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He had at that time withdrawn from them for a month.

"Umatti'kunna" (I will provide for you): i.e., the lawful provision (mut'ah) due upon divorce, according to the circumstances of the divorcing husband, in abundance or in scarcity.

"Usarrihkunna sarahan jamilan" (And release you with a fair release): i.e., I will divorce you without causing you harm.

"Turidna Allaha wa rasulahu wa al-dar al-akhirah" (If you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode): i.e., you desire the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger and Paradise.

"Fa-inna Allaha a'adda lil-muhsinat" (Indeed, Allah has prepared for the good-doers): i.e., the company of the Prophet (ﷺ), in addition to general goodness.

"Bi-fahishatin mubayyinah" (With a manifest indecency): i.e., with a disobedience of character by which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be hurt.

"Yudaa'af laha al-'adhab di'fayn" (Her punishment will be doubled twofold): i.e., twice over the punishment of others who harmed their husbands.

"Wa kana dhalika 'ala Allahi yasiran" (And that is ever easy for Allah): i.e., doubling the punishment is easy and effortless for Allah, exalted is He.

Meaning of the verses:

It was the will of Allah, exalted is He, that the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ), when they saw that the women of the Ansar and the Muhajirin had been given more in maintenance, owing to the ease and abundance of provision among the people of Madinah, should ask for an increase in their maintenance, on a par with others. At that time they were nine: 'A'ishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint 'Umar, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah, and Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadriyyah. 'A'ishah informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of this, and he was distressed by it, since he had no ability to meet what was asked of him. He sat in his upper chamber (mashrabah) and withdrew from them for a full month, until Allah revealed the verse of choice, which is this: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment﴾, of delicious food and drink, fine clothing, adornments of jewelry, and abundance of all of that; then come, to the lofty station of the Messenger. ﴿I will provide for you﴾, the lawful provision upon divorce, ﴿and release you with a fair release﴾, i.e., without any harm accompanying it. ﴿But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾, i.e., their pleasure, and the Garden ﴿then indeed Allah has prepared﴾, i.e., readied and made present, ﴿for the good-doers among you﴾ in obedience to Allah and His Messenger ﴿a great reward﴾, which is the high ranks in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Abode of Peace.

The Prophet (ﷺ) gave them the choice in compliance with the command of Allah in His words ﴿Say to your wives﴾, and he began with 'A'ishah and said to her: "I want to mention a matter to you, and you should not decide on it until you consult your two parents," i.e., seek their opinion in this matter. Then he recited the verse to her, and she chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. The others followed her in this, and none of them chose other than Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. Allah honored them for that, and revealed to His Messenger: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever, over all things, an Watcher﴾ [al-Ahzab: 52].

And His words, ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a manifest indecency﴾, i.e., a clear, evil trait, such as bad conduct toward the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿her punishment will be doubled﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, because harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among the gateways to disbelief, and Allah forbid. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾, i.e., doubling the punishment of the one who commits a manifest indecency is a small matter for Allah, which does not hinder Him from doing it. This is for two reasons: first, because harming the Messenger is among the gateways to disbelief; second, because of their lofty rank and nobility. For one of high station and lofty standing, a wrong is judged more harshly than it would be from others.

Guidance from the verses:

1) The legitimacy of giving wives the choice: if they choose divorce, they are divorced; if they do not choose it, no divorce takes place.

2) The perfection of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), in that they chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode over the world and its adornment.

3) The legitimacy of provision (mut'ah) after divorce, which is giving the woman some wealth according to the wealth and poverty of the divorcing husband, based on His words ﴿upon the wealthy according to his means, and upon the poor according to his means﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236].

4) The obligation of general and particular goodness: particular, toward husband and wife; general, in obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

5) The clarification that the wrongdoing of a noble scholar is worse than the wrongdoing of a lowly ignorant person. For this reason they said: "The good deeds of the righteous are the misdeeds of those brought near," a well-known saying used for admonition and reflection.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 33, verses 31–34:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"And whoever of you devotes herself (yaqnut) to Allah and His Messenger":* that is, whoever of you obeys Allah and His Messenger.

*"We will give her reward twice":* that is, We will multiply the reward of her righteous deeds so that it is double the reward of another woman who is not one of the wives of the Prophet.

*"And We have prepared for her a noble provision":* that is, in Paradise.

*"O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women":* that is, you are not, in virtue, like the general body of women.

*"If you fear Allah":* rather, you are more honoured and more excellent, on condition of your piety toward Allah.

*"So do not be soft in speech":* that is, in view of your nobility, do not soften your speech.

*"So that he in whose heart is a disease will covet":* that is, the disease of hypocrisy (nifaq) or the disease of desire.

*"And speak with appropriate speech":* that is, the custom is to speak in a firm voice with no softness in it.

*"And stay in your houses":* that is, remain in your homes and do not go out except for a necessity.

*"And do not display yourselves as in the display of the former Jahiliyya":* that is, do not adorn yourselves and go out swaggering and flirtatious, as the women of the first Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to do.

*"Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity":* that is, He has only commanded you with what He has commanded, of chastity, hijab, and staying in your homes, so as to purify you from defilements and vices.

*"And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom":* that is, the Book and the Sunnah, so that you may thank Allah for this by obeying Him and His Messenger.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with the wives of the Prophet, the Mothers of the Believers (Ummahat al-Mu'minin). After they chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode over the life of this world and its adornment, they became persons of elevated rank and standing with Allah, with His Messenger, and with the believers. The Lord, blessed and exalted, informed them with His words: ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: whoever of you obeys Allah by performing His commands and abstaining from His prohibitions, and obeys His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), not disobeying him in any command and not wronging him in his companionship, and does righteous deeds of supererogation and good works, ﴿We will give her reward twice﴾, meaning We will multiply the reward of her deeds, so that it will be double the reward of another woman among women other than the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ). His words ﴿And We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾ mean in Paradise. This is a glad tiding of Paradise for the wives of the Prophet, the Mothers of the Believers, the nine, concerning whom these verses were revealed.

This is what the first verse [31] indicates. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of the women, if you are mindful of Allah﴾, meaning: O wives of the Prophet, Mothers of the Believers, you are not like the general body of women, if your nobility is greater and your station higher. And how could it be otherwise, when you are the Mothers of the Believers and the wives of the Seal of the Prophets? So recognize your worth by increasing your obedience to Allah and His Messenger. His words *"if you fear Allah"* mean: this honour has been attained by you through your piety toward Allah, so hold fast to piety, for without piety your standing is nothing, and your situation is like that of the rest of women. Accordingly, ﴿do not be soft in speech﴾, meaning: do not soften your words or make your voices tender when you speak with men who are not related to you. His exalted saying ﴿so that he in whose heart is a disease will covet﴾ refers to hypocrisy or weakness of faith combined with raging desire, which causes him to take pleasure in the address. And His saying ﴿and speak with appropriate speech﴾ means speech that conveys the required meaning without excess words and expressions that are not needed.

His saying ﴿and stay in your houses﴾ means: remain in them, that is, keep to them, and do not go out except for a necessity that cannot be avoided. His saying ﴿and do not display yourselves﴾ means: when you go out for a necessity ﴿as in the display of the former Jahiliyya﴾, that is, before Islam, when a woman would adorn herself, go out swaggering and coquettish, and move and speak in a seductive manner, enticing men.

His exalted saying ﴿and establish prayer﴾ means perform it with all its conditions, pillars, and obligations completed, at its appointed times, with humble submission (khushu') in it; ﴿and give zakah﴾ and ﴿obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ by carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. He commanded them with the foundations of Islam and its most important pillars. His saying: ﴿Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ means: We have only commanded you and forbidden you, intending to remove defilement and sin, to preserve your purity, O people of the Prophet's household.

His exalted saying ﴿and purify you with complete purification﴾ means complete and thorough purification from everything that is sinful and that corrupts and defiles the soul.

His exalted saying ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾ refers to the Book and the Sunnah. This is a command to them by way of admonition and a reminder of the multiplicity of blessings.

His exalted saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾ means: Subtle toward you, O people of the household, and Aware of your circumstances. So trust in Him and entrust the matter to Him. The intended meaning of "people of the household" here includes the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), Fatimah, her two sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and 'Ali, the noble son-in-law. May Allah be pleased with the Family of the Messenger of Allah, all of them, and with his Companions, ukta'in, abta'in, absa'in (all of them).

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. There is no honour except through piety. "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you."

2. Explanation of the virtue and nobility of the wives of the Prophet.

3. The prohibition on a woman softening her voice and making her speech tender when speaking with a non-relative man.

4. The obligation for women to remain in their homes and not go out except for a necessity that cannot be avoided.

5. The prohibition of tabarruj (ostentatious display), which is when a woman adorns herself and goes out showing her attractions, swaggering in her walk.

6. A Muslim should remember the honour Allah has bestowed upon him through faith and Islam, so that he may rise above base and vile conduct.

7. An indication that wisdom refers to the authentic Sunnah of the Prophet.

8. A reference to the existence of a second Jahiliyya, which has appeared within the last half century, namely women's display by uncovering the head, chest, legs, and even thighs.

*"So that he in whose heart is a disease will covet":* that is, the disease of hypocrisy (nifaq) or the disease of desire.

*"And speak with appropriate speech":* that is, the custom is to speak in a firm voice with no softness in it.

*"And stay in your houses":* that is, remain in your homes and do not go out except for a necessity.

*"And do not display yourselves as in the display of the former Jahiliyya":* that is, do not adorn yourselves and go out swaggering and flirtatious, as the women of the first Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to do.

*"Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity":* that is, He has only commanded you with what He has commanded, of chastity, hijab, and staying in your homes, so as to purify you from defilements and vices.

The noble context continues with the wives of the Prophet, the Mothers of the Believers (Ummahat al-Mu'minin). After they chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode over the life of this world and its adornment, they became persons of elevated rank and standing with Allah, with His Messenger, and with the believers. His words ﴿And We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾ mean in Paradise. This is what the first verse [31] indicates. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of the women, if you are mindful of Allah﴾, meaning: O wives of the Prophet, Mothers of the Believers, you are not like the general body of women, if your nobility is greater and your station higher. And how could it be otherwise, when you are the Mothers of the Believers and the wives of the Seal of the Prophets? So recognize your worth by increasing your obedience to Allah and His Messenger. His words *"if you fear Allah"* mean: this honour has been attained by you through your piety toward Allah, so hold fast to piety, for without piety your standing is nothing, and your situation is like that of the rest of women. Accordingly, ﴿do not be soft in speech﴾, meaning: do not soften your words or make your voices tender when you speak with men who are not related to you. His exalted saying ﴿so that he in whose heart is a disease will covet﴾ refers to hypocrisy or weakness of faith combined with raging desire, which causes him to take pleasure in the address. And His saying ﴿and speak with appropriate speech﴾ means speech that conveys the required meaning without excess words and expressions that are not needed.

His saying ﴿and stay in your houses﴾ means: remain in them, that is, keep to them, and do not go out except for a necessity that cannot be avoided. His saying ﴿and do not display yourselves﴾ means: when you go out for a necessity ﴿as in the display of the former Jahiliyya﴾, that is, before Islam, when a woman would adorn herself, go out swaggering and coquettish, and move and speak in a seductive manner, enticing men.

His exalted saying ﴿and establish prayer﴾ means perform it with all its conditions, pillars, and obligations completed, at its appointed times, with humble submission (khushu') in it; ﴿and give zakah﴾ and ﴿obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ by carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. He commanded them with the foundations of Islam and its most important pillars. His saying: ﴿Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ means: We have only commanded you and forbidden you, intending to remove defilement and sin, to preserve your purity, O people of the Prophet's household.

His exalted saying ﴿and purify you with complete purification﴾ means complete and thorough purification from everything that is sinful and that corrupts and defiles the soul.

His exalted saying ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾ refers to the Book and the Sunnah. This is a command to them by way of admonition and a reminder of the multiplicity of blessings.

His exalted saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾ means: Subtle toward you, O people of the household, and Aware of your circumstances. So trust in Him and entrust the matter to Him. The intended meaning of "people of the household" here includes the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), Fatimah, her two sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and 'Ali, the noble son-in-law. May Allah be pleased with the Family of the Messenger of Allah, all of them, and with his Companions, ukta'in, abta'in, absa'in (all of them).

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. There is no honour except through piety. "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you."

2. Explanation of the virtue and nobility of the wives of the Prophet.

3. The prohibition on a woman softening her voice and making her speech tender when speaking with a non-relative man.

4. The obligation for women to remain in their homes and not go out except for a necessity that cannot be avoided.

5. The prohibition of tabarruj (ostentatious display), which is when a woman adorns herself and goes out showing her attractions, swaggering in her walk.

6. A Muslim should remember the honour Allah has bestowed upon him through faith and Islam, so that he may rise above base and vile conduct.

7. An indication that wisdom refers to the authentic Sunnah of the Prophet.

8. A reference to the existence of a second Jahiliyya, which has appeared within the last half century, namely women's display by uncovering the head, chest, legs, and even thighs.
