Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verse 35:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Inna al-muslimina wal-muslimat﴾: Indeed, those who submit to God, turning their faces to Him, complying with God outwardly and inwardly, and likewise the (female) Muslims.

﴿wal-mu'minina wal-mu'minat﴾: That is, those who affirm belief in God as Lord and God, and in the Prophet Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and in Islam as religion and law, and likewise the (female) believers.

﴿wal-qanitina wal-qanitat﴾: That is, the men who obey God and His Messenger, and the women who obey.

﴿wal-sadiqina wal-sadiqat﴾: That is, those who are truthful in their words and deeds, and likewise the (female) truthful.

﴿wal-sabirina wal-sabirat﴾: That is, those who restrain their souls from abandoning acts of obedience, from approaching acts of disobedience, and in affliction, do not express anger at it or complain to God's servants about God; and likewise the (female) patient.

﴿wal-khashi'ina wal-khashi'at﴾: That is, those who humble themselves before God and are submissive to Him, and likewise the women who are humble.

﴿wal-mutasaddiqina wal-mutasaddiqat﴾: That is, those who pay zakat and give surplus of their wealth when there is need for it, and likewise the women who pay.

﴿wal-hafizina furujahum﴾: That is, who guard against what is forbidden, and likewise the women who guard, except before their spouses or what their right hands possess, in regard to men; as for women, they guard their private parts except before their spouses only.

﴿wal-dhakirina Allaha kathiran wal-dhakirat﴾: That is, with tongues and hearts. At a minimum, they remember God three hundred times in the day and night, in addition to remembering God in the five prayers.

﴿A'adda Allahu lahum maghfiratan﴾: That is, forgiveness for their sins and the sins of the women.

﴿wa-ajran 'aziman﴾: That is, Paradise, the abode of the righteous.

Meaning of the verses:

This verse, though it was revealed in answer to a question from some of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, who said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Why are we not mentioned in the Qur'an as men are mentioned?" God the Most High then revealed this blessed verse, ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...﴾. Its connection to what precedes it is clear: when He praised the Family of the House with goodness, the souls of the Muslim men and women longed for a good like that which the pure Family of the House had attained. So God mentioned that the Muslim men and women are those who submit to the command of God and His Messenger, who have turned their faces to God and so do not turn to other than Him; like the believing men and women who affirm God as Lord and God, Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and Islam as religion and law; like the obedient men and women, that is, those who obey God and His Messenger in ease and hardship, in what is liked and what is disliked, within the limits of human capacity; like the truthful in their words and deeds, and the truthful women; like the patient, that is, those who restrain their souls upon acts of obedience in deed, and from forbidden things by abstaining, and in affliction by contentment and submission; and the patient women; like the humble in their prayers and all their acts of worship, and the women who are humble before God the Most High; like those who give charity by paying the zakat of their wealth and its surplus when there is need for it, and the women who give charity; like those who fast Ramadan and voluntary fasts such as Ashura, and the women who fast; like those who guard their private parts from what God has forbidden to them of intercourse and from exposing them to other than spouses, and the women who guard; like those who remember God much by night and day, remembrance of the heart and tongue, and the women who remember—all of them. God the Most High has prepared for them forgiveness for their sins, since they had sins, and a great reward, that is, a great recompense for their acts of obedience after their faith, which is Paradise, the abode of peace. May God make us among them and among the people of Paradise.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of the verses:

1- Good news to the Muslim men and Muslim women of forgiveness of their sins and entry into Paradise if they possess those described qualities in this verse, which are ten qualities, the first of which is Islam and the last of which is the remembrance of God the Most High.

2- The excellence of the qualities mentioned, since they are a cause of entering Paradise after the forgiveness of sins.

3- Affirmation of the principle of equality between men and women in deed and reward. In the deeds that God the Most High has assigned to women and men together, and as for what is specific to men or to women, then for men there is a share of what they have earned and for women a share of what they have earned, and God says the truth and guides to the way.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 36–40:

Explanation of the words:

*Ma kana li-mu'minin wa la mu'minatin*: That is, it is not fitting or proper for a believing man or a believing woman.

*An yakuna lahumu al-khiyara min amrihim*: That is, the right to choose in a matter about which Allah and His Messenger have decided, whether permitting or forbidding it.

*Faqad dalla dalalan mubinan*: That is, he has clearly erred from the path of salvation and success.

*An'ama Allahu 'alayhi wa an'amta 'alayhi*: That is, Allah bestowed on him Islam, and you bestowed on him manumission, and he is Zayd ibn Harithah.

*Wa-attaqi Allah*: That is, regarding the matter of your wife, do not try to divorce her.

*Wa tukhfi fi nafsika*: That is, and you conceal within yourself, namely your knowledge that when Zayd divorces Zaynab, Allah will marry her to you, nullifying what people held regarding the prohibition of marrying the wife of an adopted son.

*Ma Allahu mubdihi*: That is, He will certainly make it manifest, namely the Messenger's marriage to Zaynab after her divorce.

*Wa takhsha al-nas*: That is, lest they say, "Muhammad married the divorced wife of his freedman Zayd."

*Wa Allahu ahaqqu an takhshahu*: He is the One who willed that marriage for you.

*Falamma qada Zaydun minha wataran*: That is, once he had fulfilled his need of her, he no longer had any desire for her, because of her haughtiness toward him due to the nobility of her lineage and the honour of her forefathers.

*Zawwajnakaha*: For Allah Himself undertook the contract of her marriage. The Prophet ﷺ then entered upon her without the permission of anyone, and that was in the fifth year, and people were fed meat and bread at the wedding feast for her.

*Likay la yakuna 'ala al-mu'minina haraj*: That is, no sin for them in marrying the divorced wives of their adopted sons.

*Wa kana amru Allahi mafulan*: That is, what Allah has decreed in the Preserved Tablet must occur without fail.

*Wa la yakhshawna ahadan illa Allah*: That is, they act upon what their Lord has permitted them and do not heed the words of people.

*Wa kafa billahi hasiban*: That is, He is the Guardian over the deeds of His servants and the Reckoner of them on the Day of Reckoning.

*Ma kana Muhammadun abā ahadin min rijalikum*: That is, he was not the father of Zayd or of any other man, since his male children died while they were young.

*Wa khatam al-nabiyyin*: That is, no prophet came after him. For had a prophet come after him, his son would have been fit for prophethood, as were the sons of Abraham and Jacob, and David, for example.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted said: *"Wa ma kana li-mu'minin wa la mu'minatin..."* This begins the account of the marriage of Zayd ibn Harithah al-Kalbi, freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to Zaynab bint Jahsh, daughter of the Prophet's paternal aunt Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib. When Allah nullified adoption and prohibited it by His words, *"Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons"* [al-Ahzab: 4], and His words, *"Call them by their fathers' names"* [al-Ahzab: 5], there followed from that that an adopted son does not inherit from the one who adopted him, and that the divorced wife of an adopted son is not forbidden to the one who adopted him. Thus the rulings that were binding upon adoption were abolished. That the Qur'an revealed this was not easy for souls that had become accustomed to these rulings in the Jahiliyyah and the early period of Islam to accept and submit to readily. So Allah the Exalted willed to bring that into existence, and He inspired His Messenger to propose Zaynab for his freedman Zayd. Zaynab accepted the proposal, understanding that she was being proposed to the Messenger of Allah so that she might become a mother of the believers. But after some nights it became clear to her that she was being proposed to Zayd ibn Harithah, freedman of the Messenger of Allah, and it was not as she had understood. Pride seized her, and she said, "This will not be; I will not marry a noblewoman to a freedman of the people." Her brother, Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, supported her in this.

Then this verse was revealed: *"Wa ma kana li-mu'minin wa la mu'minatin idha qada Allahu wa rasuluhu amran an yakuna lahumu al-khiyara min amrihim..."* Thereupon she accepted the marriage to Zayd willingly, and Zayd married her. But by the nature of human dispositions, Zaynab did not conceal her nobility from Zayd, and she began to act haughtily toward him, so that Zayd felt there was no benefit in this marriage. He began to consult the Messenger of Allah, his master, and to seek his permission to divorce her, while the Messenger refused him, knowing that if he divorced her, Allah would marry her to him, thereby putting an end to the matter of making the rulings of adoption like those of a son by birth. So he would say to him, "Fear Allah, O Zayd; do not divorce without necessity or need for divorce, and bear patiently what you find from your wife."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 41–44:

Explanation of the words:

"O you who have believed": that is, O you who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad as Messenger.

"Remember Allah with much remembrance": that is, with your hearts and your tongues.

"And exalt Him morning and evening": that is, declare Him far above imperfection by saying "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to Allah) and "wa bihamdihi" (and with His praise), in the morning and in the evening.

"It is He who sends blessings upon you": that is, who shows mercy to you.

"And His angels": that is, they seek forgiveness for you.

"That He may bring you out of darknesses": that is, He shows mercy to you so as to continually bring you out of the darknesses of disbelief into the light of faith.

"Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, 'Peace'": that is, "Peace be upon you," for the angels greet them.

"And He has prepared for them a noble reward": that is, He has readied for them a noble reward, which is Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

This noble call from a Lord who is merciful is addressed to the sincere believers, to teach them what increases their faith and light, and by which they are protected from their enemy, which is the remembrance of Allah. So He, the Exalted, said to them, "O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance" (33:41), a remembrance without limit or restriction, for it is the energy that helps one toward spiritual life. "And exalt Him morning and evening" (33:42): by the prayer of dawn and the prayer of afternoon. And [say] "Subhan Allah," "al-hamdu lillah," and "Allahu akbar" after every one of the five prayers. As for His, the Exalted's, saying, "It is He who sends blessings upon you and His angels" (33:43): His blessing upon them is His mercy toward them, and the blessing of His angels is their seeking forgiveness for them. As for His saying "that He may bring you out of the darknesses," that means out of the darknesses of disbelief and sins into the light of faith and acts of obedience. So His blessing and the blessing of His angels are the cause of bringing them out of darkness into light. And His saying, "And ever has He been, toward the believers, Merciful" (33:43), is another added favour beyond the first honour, which is the blessing upon them. Indeed, He is merciful to the believers in general, so He does not punish them or make them wretched. As for His saying, "Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, 'Peace'" (33:44): that is, their greeting on the Day of Resurrection in the abode of peace will be peace, since the angels enter upon them from every gate saying, "Peace be upon you" (13:23–24), that is, safety and security for you, so there is no fear and no grief. As for His saying, "And He has prepared for them a noble reward" (33:44): that is, He has readied and made present for them a noble reward, which is Paradise. Glory be to Allah, how generous He is, and glory be to Allah, how happy the believers are. How great is the virtue of faith and of obedience to the Most Merciful! He commanded them to remember Him much and to glorify Him morning and evening, and He gave them what its worth cannot be measured. Glory be to Allah, how generous Allah is. And praise be to Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation of remembering Allah much, night and day, and the obligation of glorifying Him morning and evening.

2- Clarification of Allah's favour upon the believers through His blessing upon them, the blessing of His angels, and His mercy toward them.

3- Affirmation of the belief in resurrection by mentioning some of what takes place in it, such as the angels' greeting to the people of Paradise.

4- Good tidings to the sincere believers of Paradise.

Wa da'iyan ila Allah bi-idhnihi (and one who calls to God by His leave): i.e., calling to faith in God, to His Oneness, and to obedience to Him by His command, may He be exalted.

Wa sirajan muniran (and a radiant lamp): i.e., and He made you like a radiant lamp by which whoever wishes guidance to the path of success is guided.

Wa la tuti' al-kafirin wa al-munafiqin (and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites): i.e., in whatever contradicts the command of your Lord and what He has legislated for you and for your community.

Wa da' adhahum (and disregard their harm): i.e., leave off their harm, do not respond to it with another harm, until you are commanded concerning them.

Wa tawakkal 'ala Allah (and put your trust in God): i.e., entrust your affair to Him, for He will suffice you.

Meaning of the verses:

This is a particular address following the general address before it; the first was for the believers, with the Messenger as their leader at their head. This is a particular address for the further honouring, ennobling and charging of the Messenger. Thus the Exalted says: ﴿O Prophet﴾ — Muhammad (ﷺ) — ﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾ as a witness over those to whom We sent you, bearing witness on the Day of Resurrection over those who answered your call and those who did not; and as a bringer of good news to whoever responds to you, believes and does righteous deeds, of Paradise; and as a warner to whoever turns away, does not believe and does not do good, of the punishment of the Fire; and as one who calls to God, the Exalted, His servants to Him, that they may believe in Him, affirm His Oneness and obey Him by His command, the Exalted, to you in that; and as a radiant lamp by which whoever seeks guidance to the path of happiness and perfection is guided through you.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, i.e., look after your calling to them, and give good tidings to those of them who believe, namely those who responded to you, believed and did righteous deeds, that for them from God is a great bounty, namely the forgiveness of their sins and their admission into Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss and complete peace. As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ in what they propose to you of matters that conflict with your call and your mission; ﴿and disregard their harm﴾, i.e., leave off harming them and be patient with them until your Lord commands you concerning what you should do towards them; ﴿and put your trust in God in all your affairs, for He suffices you, and God is sufficient as a Guardian﴾, i.e., a protector and defender who shields you from people.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance from these verses:

1- An explanation of the Muhammadan perfection with which his Lord, blessed and exalted, endowed him.

2- The legitimacy of calling to God when the caller is qualified with knowledge and forbearance, and these two are the permission (al-idhn).

3- The prohibition of obeying the disbelievers, hypocrites, sinners and wrongdoers in what contradicts the good pleasure of God, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verse 49:

Explanation of the words:

"O you who have believed": i.e., O you who have affirmed belief in Allah, His Messenger, His Book and His law.

"When you marry believing women": i.e., when you have contracted marriage with them and have not yet consummated it.

"Before you have touched them": i.e., before seclusion with them (al-khalwa) and intercourse with them (al-wati').

"Then you have no waiting period (iddah) for them to count": i.e., you have no right to demand from them a waiting period, since the iddah is incumbent upon a woman who has been consummated with.

"Then provide for them": i.e., give them some wealth which they may enjoy, as a consolation for their hearts.

"And release them with a fair release": i.e., let them go so that they may depart to their families without harming them.

The meaning of the noble verse:

Allah, exalted is He, calls His believing servants and, instructing them as a lawgiver, says: ﴿When you marry believing women﴾, i.e., you contract marriage with them, ﴿then divorce them before you have touched them﴾, i.e., before going in to them, which is accomplished by seclusion on the bed, ﴿then you have no waiting period for them to count﴾, which you could reckon against them, neither by menstrual cycles nor by months, since the iddah is for knowing what is in the womb, and the one not consummated with is known to have an empty womb. If you have specified a dower for them, then they are entitled to half of the specified amount, and the provision (al-mut'ah) is recommended. If you have not specified a dower for them, then they have nothing but the provision, which here is obligatory for them according to the wealth or poverty of the divorcing husband. And His saying: ﴿And release them with a fair release﴾, i.e., let them go their way, so that they depart to their relatives without harm to them and without any injury that you inflict upon them.

Guidance from the noble verse:

Among the guidance of the noble verse:

1- The permissibility of divorce before consummation.

2- A woman divorced before consummation has no iddah; rather, she may marry at the moment she is divorced.

3- A woman divorced before consummation: if a dower was specified for her, she is entitled to half of it; if no dower was specified for her, then the provision is obligatory for her, to be assessed by the judge according to the means of the divorcing husband, whether wealthy or straitened.

4- The prohibition of harming a divorced woman in any way, and the obligation of releasing her to go wherever she wishes.

5- The legislated provision for every divorced woman.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verse 50:

Explanation of the words:

﴿آتيت أجورهن﴾: i.e., you gave their dowries (mahr).

﴿مما أفاء الله عليك﴾: i.e., from what is taken as spoils (yusba), such as Safiyya and Juwayriyya.

﴿اللاتي هاجرن معك﴾: i.e., unlike those who did not emigrate and remained in the abode of disbelief.

﴿وهبت نفسها للنبي﴾: i.e., and the Prophet wished to marry her, without a dowry (sadaq).

﴿خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين﴾: i.e., without a dowry.

﴿قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم﴾: i.e., upon the believers.

﴿في أزواجهم﴾: i.e., of the rulings, such as that they should not exceed four, and that they should not marry except with a guardian (wali), a dowry, and witnesses.

﴿وما ملكت أيمانهم﴾: i.e., by purchase or the like, and that the slave woman be a People of the Book (kitabiyya), and that she be purified (istibra') before intercourse.

﴿لكيلا يكون عليك حرج﴾: i.e., narrowness in marriage.

The meaning of the noble verse:

This noble address to the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds brings the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a divine permission that lightens the burdens he bears (ﷺ). Allah knew what His Messenger suffers and what he deals with of the affairs of religion and of this world, so He bestowed upon him lightening and the removal of hardship, saying, bestowing favor upon him: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whose dowries you have given﴾, i.e., their dowries; and We have made lawful for you ﴿what your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you as spoils﴾, such as Safiyya bint Huyayy and Juwayriyya bint al-Harith, ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you﴾, from Makkah to Madinah.

As for those who did not emigrate, they are not lawful to you. And a believing woman: i.e., and We have made lawful to you a believing woman, not a disbeliever, if she gives herself to the Prophet without a dowry and the Prophet wishes to marry her, while this giver is exclusively yours to the exclusion of the believers. For if a woman gave herself to a believer without a dowry, it would not be lawful for him; rather a dowry, a guardian, and witnesses are necessary.

And the words of the Most High: ﴿We have already known what We have enjoined upon them﴾, i.e., upon the believers regarding their wives, of rulings such as that a man should not exceed four, that he should not marry except with a guardian, a dowry, and witnesses, and that a slave woman must be a People of the Book or a Muslim, and that he must not have intercourse with her before istibra' by a menstrual cycle. We have known all of this, and We have made lawful for you what We have made lawful as a particular privilege for you to the exclusion of the believers, and that is a lightening upon you, ﴿so that there will be no hardship upon you﴾, i.e., narrowness and difficulty. And Allah is ever Forgiving to you and to whoever of the believers repents, and Merciful to you and to the believers.

Guidance of the verse:

Among the guidance of the verse:

1- Clarification of Allah's honoring of His Prophet by lightening (the rulings) for him out of mercy towards him: He permitted him more than four, while restricting the believers to four; and He permitted him, for a woman who gives herself, to marry her without a dowry or guardian, which was not permitted to the believers, who must have a dowry, a guardian, and witnesses.

2- Affirmation of the rulings of marriage for the believers, and that they have not been subject to abrogation (naskh), neither by lightening nor by tightening.

3- Clarification of the vastness of Allah's mercy and forgiveness towards His believing servants.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 51–52:

Explanation of the words:

"Turji man tasha'u minhunna" (You may postpone whom you will of them): i.e., you may delay [your turn with] whom you wish of your wives.

"Wa tu'wi ilayka man tasha'" (And you may take to yourself whom you wish): i.e., and you may draw to yourself whom you wish of your wives, so that you go to her.

"Wa man ibtaghayta" (And whomever you seek): i.e., whomever you desire.

"Mimman 'azalta" (Of those you had set aside): i.e., from the turn (al-qasm).

"Fala junaha 'alayk" (Then there is no blame upon you): i.e., there is no sin upon you in seeking her and drawing her to you, which her Lord gave him the choice in, after the division (al-qasm) had been obligatory upon him.

"Dhalika adna an taqarra a'yunuhunna" (That is more likely that their eyes be comforted): i.e., this choice given to you, in taking whom you wish and leaving whom you wish, is closer to their eyes being comforted and not grieving.

"Wa yardayna bima ataytahunna" (And that they be pleased with what you give them): i.e., with what you have been given the choice in, of division and leaving it, and of setting aside and taking to oneself.

"Wallahu ya'lamu ma fi qulubikum" (And Allah knows what is in your hearts): i.e., of love for women, O men, and inclination toward some over others. Allah Most High gave His Messenger this choice only as facilitation for him, because of the greatness of his responsibilities.

"Wa kana Allahu 'alimran halimа" (And Allah is ever Knowing, Forbearing): i.e., Knowing of the weakness of His creation, Forbearing toward them, not hastening punishment, and accepting repentance.

"La yahillu laka an-nisa'u min ba'd" (It is not lawful for you to [marry] women after [these]): i.e., it is not permissible for you to marry after these nine whom chose you, in honor of them and lightening for you.

"Wa la an tubaddala bihinna min azwaj" (Nor to exchange them for other wives): i.e., by divorcing some of them and marrying another in place of the divorced one. No, no.

"Wa law a'jabaka husnuhunna" (Even if their beauty pleased you): it is not proper that you divorce any of these nine and marry one whose beauty pleases you.

"Illa ma malakat yaminuka" (Except what your right hand possesses): i.e., the matter in this is broad, so there is no blame upon you for taking a slave-woman as a concubine. The Prophet ﷺ did take Mariyah as a concubine; she was a gift sent to him by the ruler of Egypt, and she bore him Ibrahim, who died in the years of his nursing, peace be upon him.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues concerning facilitation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It has already been mentioned that he was permitted to marry whom he wished of those mentioned to him, and was singled out with a woman who gives herself to him in marriage without a dowry and without a guardian. In this noble verse [51], "Turji man tasha'u minhunna" (You may postpone whom you will of them), Allah Most High made it easy for him by permitting him to withhold from intercourse whom he wishes, to postpone whom he wishes, to take to himself and join whom he wishes, and to seek whom he has set aside if he wishes; there is no blame on him in any of that. Yet he used to divide [his time] among his wives, and would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not." Except that Sawda, may Allah be pleased with her, gave her night to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her.

This is what His saying, "Turji man tasha'u minhunna wa tu'wi ilayka man tasha'u wa man ibtaghayta mimman 'azalta fala junaha 'alayk," indicates. And His saying, "Dhalika adna" means: that choice given to you regarding your wives is closer to their eyes being comforted, i.e., they will be delighted with you and will not grieve over you, and they will be pleased with what you bestow upon them of taking to yourself and of intimacy.

His saying, Exalted is He, "Wallahu ya'lamu ma fi qulubikum" means: O people, of desire for [women] in address, and a man's inclination toward some of his wives over others. Allah gave His Messenger this choice only as facilitation for him and lightening of his responsibilities, which great men would not aspire to, even if they had the strength and endurance of mountains or camels.

His saying, "Wa kana Allahu 'alimran" means: Knowing of His creation and their needs; "halimran 'alayhim" means: Forbearing toward them, not hastening punishment, and accepting repentance from whoever repents.

His saying, Exalted is He, in verse [52], "La yahillu laka an-nisa'u min ba'd" means: it is not lawful for you, O our Messenger, to take women after these nine whom you gave the choice, and they chose Allah, and chose you, and you are His Messenger, and chose the Hereafter. In recognition of their station, Allah has confined you to them from now on, so do not seek another woman, whether by exchange or without exchange. Meaning "by exchange": that he divorce one or more of them and marry in her place. This is the meaning of His saying, "Wa la an tubaddala bihinna min azwaj wa law a'jabaka husnuhunna." And His saying, "Illa ma malakat yaminuka" means: there is no harm in taking a slave-woman you own as a concubine. He did take Mariyah the Copt, whom al-Muqawqis, ruler of Egypt, gave him along with a white mule called Duldul, the first mule to enter the Hijaz. Mariyah bore Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who died in the days of his nursing, upon him and his father be a thousand thousand peaces.

His saying, Exalted is He, "Wa kana Allahu 'ala kulli shay'in raqiban" means: Watchful and All-Knowing over everything. So fear Him and be mindful of Him, and do not seek the pleasure of anyone other than Him by pleasing Him, for He is your God, besides whom you have no god; your life is by Him, and to Him is your return after your death.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's honoring of His Messenger through facilitation and ease for him because of the multitude of his responsibilities.

2- What Allah gave His Messenger the choice in is not valid for any Muslim, except that a man may say to a woman of advanced age or sickness, "So-and-so, I wish to marry, to guard myself, and you, as you know, are unable; so if you wish I will divorce you, and if you wish you may waive your night." If she chooses to remain while waiving her right in the marital bed, there is no harm in that.

3- In Allah's management of His Messenger and his wives there are benefits and interests beyond measure.

4- Affirmation of the principle: "No one leaves something for Allah except that Allah replaces it with something better." This is manifest in the choice of the wives of the Messenger ﷺ of Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter.

5- The obligation of being mindful of Allah Most High and not contemplating departure from His obedience under any circumstances.

[Important note]

Allah's permission to His Messenger ﷺ to marry more than four was for lofty wisdoms, and how not, when the Legislator is Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Among those lofty wisdoms are the following:

(1) The requirements of legislation specific to women, including what only the spouses can know, so that plurality of wives would transmit the rulings specific to women; and for the soundness and acceptance of transmission in the community, there is the multiplicity of chains and the abundance of narrators and reports.

(2) The early days of the Islamic call required powerful supporters, and none is better than the in-laws of the calling man, for by custom they stand beside their in-law, whether right or wrong.

(3) That believers have no dearer wish than to be related by marriage to the Prophet of Allah, so as to gain entry to his house and private company, and how precious that is. Which of the believers would not wish that his mother, sister, or daughter be a mother of the believers? By Allah, I love nothing more than that I, my wife, and all my children be servants in the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Therefore Allah widened [the permission] for His Messenger, so that it would at least accommodate widows and women of honor, lest their honor be defiled.

(4) The Messenger of Allah ﷺ may need to reward someone who has done him kindness and has nothing to repay him with, and sees that he desires marriage into his family, so he accepts; and from this is his marriage to both 'A'isha daughter of as-Siddiq and Hafsa daughter of al-Faruq, may Allah be pleased with them all.

(5) His Lord married him to Zaynab while he disliked it, avoiding it out of fear of people's talk, for they considered it reprehensible: marrying the wife of the adopted son after her divorce or the death of her husband. These are some of the wisdoms that required the permission for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to marry more than four, together with another important factor: the Messenger of Allah's ability to be just and sufficient, a matter that will never be possible for anyone else.

"Dhalika adna an taqarra a'yunuhunna" (That is more likely that their eyes be comforted): i.e., this choice given to you, in taking whom you wish and leaving whom you wish, is closer to their eyes being comforted and not grieving.

"Wa yardayna bima ataytahunna" (And that they be pleased with what you give them): i.e., with what you have been given the choice in, of division and leaving it, and of setting aside and taking to oneself.

"Wallahu ya'lamu ma fi qulubikum" (And Allah knows what is in your hearts): i.e., of love for women, O men, and inclination toward some over others. Allah Most High gave His Messenger this choice only as facilitation for him, because of the greatness of his responsibilities.

"Wa kana Allahu 'alimran halimа" (And Allah is ever Knowing, Forbearing): i.e., Knowing of the weakness of His creation, Forbearing toward them, not hastening punishment, and accepting repentance.

"La yahillu laka an-nisa'u min ba'd" (It is not lawful for you to [marry] women after [these]): i.e., it is not permissible for you to marry after these nine whom chose you, in honor of them and lightening for you.

"Wa la an tubaddala bihinna min azwaj" (Nor to exchange them for other wives): i.e., by divorcing some of them and marrying another in place of the divorced one. No, no.

"Wa law a'jabaka husnuhunna" (Even if their beauty pleased you): it is not proper that you divorce any of these nine and marry one whose beauty pleases you.

"Illa ma malakat yaminuka" (Except what your right hand possesses): i.e., the matter in this is broad, so there is no blame upon you for taking a slave-woman as a concubine. The Prophet ﷺ did take Mariyah as a concubine; she was a gift sent to him by the ruler of Egypt, and she bore him Ibrahim, who died in the years of his nursing, peace be upon him.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues concerning facilitation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It has already been mentioned that he was permitted to marry whom he wished of those mentioned to him, and was singled out with a woman who gives herself to him in marriage without a dowry and without a guardian. In this noble verse [51], "Turji man tasha'u minhunna" (You may postpone whom you will of them), Allah Most High made it easy for him by permitting him to withhold from intercourse whom he wishes, to postpone whom he wishes, to take to himself and join whom he wishes, and to seek whom he has set aside if he wishes; there is no blame on him in any of that. Yet he used to divide [his time] among his wives, and would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not." Except that Sawda, may Allah be pleased with her, gave her night to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her.

This is what His saying, "Turji man tasha'u minhunna wa tu'wi ilayka man tasha'u wa man ibtaghayta mimman 'azalta fala junaha 'alayk," indicates. And His saying, "Dhalika adna" means: that choice given to you regarding your wives is closer to their eyes being comforted, i.e., they will be delighted with you and will not grieve over you, and they will be pleased with what you bestow upon them of taking to yourself and of intimacy.

His saying, Exalted is He, "Wallahu ya'lamu ma fi qulubikum" means: O people, of desire for [women] in address, and a man's inclination toward some of his wives over others. Allah gave His Messenger this choice only as facilitation for him and lightening of his responsibilities, which great men would not aspire to, even if they had the strength and endurance of mountains or camels.

His saying, "Wa kana Allahu 'alimran" means: Knowing of His creation and their needs; "halimran 'alayhim" means: Forbearing toward them, not hastening punishment, and accepting repentance from whoever repents.

His saying, Exalted is He, in verse [52], "La yahillu laka an-nisa'u min ba'd" means: it is not lawful for you, O our Messenger, to take women after these nine whom you gave the choice, and they chose Allah, and chose you, and you are His Messenger, and chose the Hereafter. In recognition of their station, Allah has confined you to them from now on, so do not seek another woman, whether by exchange or without exchange. Meaning "by exchange": that he divorce one or more of them and marry in her place. This is the meaning of His saying, "Wa la an tubaddala bihinna min azwaj wa law a'jabaka husnuhunna." And His saying, "Illa ma malakat yaminuka" means: there is no harm in taking a slave-woman you own as a concubine. He did take Mariyah the Copt, whom al-Muqawqis, ruler of Egypt, gave him along with a white mule called Duldul, the first mule to enter the Hijaz. Mariyah bore Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who died in the days of his nursing, upon him and his father be a thousand thousand peaces.

His saying, Exalted is He, "Wa kana Allahu 'ala kulli shay'in raqiban" means: Watchful and All-Knowing over everything. So fear Him and be mindful of Him, and do not seek the pleasure of anyone other than Him by pleasing Him, for He is your God, besides whom you have no god; your life is by Him, and to Him is your return after your death.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's honoring of His Messenger through facilitation and ease for him because of the multitude of his responsibilities.

2- What Allah gave His Messenger the choice in is not valid for any Muslim, except that a man may say to a woman of advanced age or sickness, "So-and-so, I wish to marry, to guard myself, and you, as you know, are unable; so if you wish I will divorce you, and if you wish you may waive your night." If she chooses to remain while waiving her right in the marital bed, there is no harm in that.

3- In Allah's management of His Messenger and his wives there are benefits and interests beyond measure.

4- Affirmation of the principle: "No one leaves something for Allah except that Allah replaces it with something better." This is manifest in the choice of the wives of the Messenger ﷺ of Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter.

5- The obligation of being mindful of Allah Most High and not contemplating departure from His obedience under any circumstances.

[Important note]

Allah's permission to His Messenger ﷺ to marry more than four was for lofty wisdoms, and how not, when the Legislator is Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Among those lofty wisdoms are the following:

(1) The requirements of legislation specific to women, including what only the spouses can know, so that plurality of wives would transmit the rulings specific to women; and for the soundness and acceptance of transmission in the community, there is the multiplicity of chains and the abundance of narrators and reports.

(2) The early days of the Islamic call required powerful supporters, and none is better than the in-laws of the calling man, for by custom they stand beside their in-law, whether right or wrong.

(3) That believers have no dearer wish than to be related by marriage to the Prophet of Allah, so as to gain entry to his house and private company, and how precious that is. Which of the believers would not wish that his mother, sister, or daughter be a mother of the believers? By Allah, I love nothing more than that I, my wife, and all my children be servants in the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Therefore Allah widened [the permission] for His Messenger, so that it would at least accommodate widows and women of honor, lest their honor be defiled.

(4) The Messenger of Allah ﷺ may need to reward someone who has done him kindness and has nothing to repay him with, and sees that he desires marriage into his family, so he accepts; and from this is his marriage to both 'A'isha daughter of as-Siddiq and Hafsa daughter of al-Faruq, may Allah be pleased with them all.

(5) His Lord married him to Zaynab while he disliked it, avoiding it out of fear of people's talk, for they considered it reprehensible: marrying the wife of the adopted son after her divorce or the death of her husband. These are some of the wisdoms that required the permission for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to marry more than four, together with another important factor: the Messenger of Allah's ability to be just and sufficient, a matter that will never be possible for anyone else.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verse 53–55:

Explanation of the words:

"O you who have believed": i.e., O you who have affirmed Allah, His promise and His threat, and the Messenger and what he brought.

"Unless permission is given to you": i.e., to enter, by being invited to a meal.

"Without waiting for its preparation (ināh)": i.e., without waiting for the time of its readiness; so do not enter before the time of the food's being brought and the guests being assembled for it, such that one of you takes advantage of the permission to be invited to the meal, comes before the time and sits in the house, thereby troubling the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his household.

"But when you have eaten, disperse": i.e., when you have eaten the food and finished, disperse, returning to your houses or your work, and let none of you remain.

"Nor lingering for conversation": i.e., do not remain lingering for the conversation of one another.

"Indeed, that would cause harm to the Prophet": i.e., that staying in the houses of the Prophet would cause harm to the Prophet ﷺ.

"And he is shy of you": i.e., of asking you to leave.

"But Allah is not shy of the truth": i.e., of stating it and commanding it; therefore He has commanded you to leave.

"From behind a screen": i.e., a cover such as a door, a curtain or the like.

"That is purer for your hearts and their hearts": i.e., from corrupt thoughts.

"Indeed, that is, in the sight of Allah, an enormity": i.e., your harm to the Messenger of Allah is, in the sight of Allah, a great sin.

"Whether you show anything or conceal it": i.e., whether you display a desire to marry the wives of the Messenger after his death, or conceal it within your souls, Allah will surely recompense you with the worst of recompense.

"There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, etc.": i.e., there is no blame upon the wives of the Prophet in showing themselves to their mahrams mentioned in the verse.

"Nor their women": i.e., the believing women; as for the non-believing women, no.

"Nor those their right hands possess": i.e., from the female slaves and male slaves, in being seen by them and being seen without a veil.

"And fear Allah": i.e., O wives of the Prophet, regarding what you have been commanded concerning the veil and other matters.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, Exalted, explained to His Messenger what is proper for him to observe concerning his wives, the Mothers of the Believers, He explained in this verse [54] what is also obligatory for the believers to observe toward the wives of the Prophet, their mothers. So He said: "O you who have believed," truly and sincerely, "do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you" to enter for a meal you are being fed, "without waiting for its preparation," i.e., its time. This verse, known as the verse of the veil, was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who, after eating the wedding feast that the Messenger held when Allah married him to Zaynab bint Jahsh (may Allah be pleased with her), and before the veil had been prescribed for women, remained after the people had left, talking. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and went out before them, hoping they would leave, but they did not leave. The Messenger repeatedly went into the house and came out, hoping they would leave with him, but they did not leave, and he ﷺ was too shy to say to them, "Come on, leave." So Allah revealed this verse. His saying, "without waiting for its preparation," refers to that group and whoever wishes to do their deed: when his brother invites him to a wedding feast after noon, for example, he comes to the house before noon and troubles the people of the house. This is the meaning of "without waiting for its preparation," i.e., its time, because "ināh" means the time.

His saying, "But when you are invited, enter," i.e., do not enter without an invitation or permission. "But when you have eaten," i.e., when you have finished eating, "disperse," going out in different directions upon the earth: this one to his house, that one to his Lord's house, and another to his work. His saying: "Nor lingering for conversation," i.e., do not remain after the meal conversing with one another, lingering in conversation. Allah, Exalted, has forbidden this to you, O believers, because it troubles His Messenger. Although the Messenger, because of the perfection of his character, does not command you to leave out of shyness toward you, Allah is not shy of the truth, so He has commanded you to leave after the meal, out of regard for the station of His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ. His saying, Exalted: "And when you ask them for an article," i.e., when you request some item of household goods, such as a vessel or the like, "then ask them from behind a screen," i.e., a door, a curtain or the like, not face to face, out of respect for the sanctity of looking at them. His saying, "That is purer for your hearts and their hearts," i.e., you men and they, O women, are purer from corrupt evil thoughts that no human heart is free of when a man speaks with a woman or a woman speaks with a man.

His saying, Exalted: "And it is not for you" to harm the Messenger of Allah in any way, nor to marry his wives after him, i.e., nor to marry his wives after his death, for they are forbidden to men with the prohibition of mothers, a permanent prohibition that is never lawful under any circumstance. His saying, Exalted: "Indeed, that," i.e., the aforementioned harm to the Messenger of Allah and marrying his wives after him, "was in the sight of Allah," i.e., in His judgment, decree and law, "a great sin," whose extent cannot be measured and whose reward and punishment none knows but Allah.

This is what the first verse [53] indicates. As for His saying, Exalted, "Whether you show anything or conceal it," i.e., you reveal it or hide it, meaning a desire to marry the wives of the Messenger after his death ﷺ, "indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing." He will surely recompense you for that desire, whether you have displayed it or concealed it within your souls, with the worst and most evil recompense. So fear Allah and venerate what He has venerated of the sacred rights of His Messenger ﷺ. This is what verse [54] indicates.

As for His saying, Exalted, in verse [55]: "There is no blame upon them," i.e., no restriction, no hardship and no sin upon the believing women, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and other women of the believers, "concerning their fathers," i.e., their fathers and grandfathers however high, "or their sons," i.e., sons and sons' sons however low, and sons of daughters likewise however low, "or their brothers," and sons of their brothers however low, and sons of their sisters however low, "or their women," and "those their right hands possess," i.e., female slaves and male slaves, that they may show their faces and speak without a veil, face to face.

His saying, Exalted: "And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness," is a command from Allah to the wives of the Prophet and the wives of the believers to fear Allah regarding what He has forbidden them and made unlawful for them, namely displaying their faces to non-mahram strangers mentioned in the verse, and a reminder of Allah's witnessing of all things and His knowledge of all things, so that this may serve as an aid to piety.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Explanation of the manners that believers must observe in seeking permission and entering houses for the purpose of a meal or the like.

2- Explanation of the perfection of the Messenger ﷺ in his character, in that he was too shy to say to his guest, "Get out of the house, the meal has ended."

3- Allah, Exalted, described Himself as not being shy of the truth in stating it and commanding it to His servants.

4- The permissibility of addressing a non-mahram woman from behind a screen, curtain or the like.

5- The prohibition of harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that it is a major crime that is not equal to any other.

6- Explanation that a person is not free of evil thoughts when he speaks to a woman and looks at her.

7- The prohibition of marrying the wives of the Messenger after his death, and the prohibition of entertaining a thought of it.

8- Explanation of the mahrams before whom a Muslim woman may uncover her face and speak without a veil.

9- The command to piety and Allah's warning to whoever does not fear Him regarding His prohibitions.

As for His saying, Exalted, in verse [55]: "There is no blame upon them," i.e., no restriction, no hardship and no sin upon the believing women, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and other women of the believers, "concerning their fathers," i.e., their fathers and grandfathers however high, "or their sons," i.e., sons and sons' sons however low, and sons of daughters likewise however low, "or their brothers," and sons of their brothers however low, and sons of their sisters however low, "or their women," and "those their right hands possess," i.e., female slaves and male slaves, that they may show their faces and speak without a veil, face to face.

His saying, Exalted: "And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness," is a command from Allah to the wives of the Prophet and the wives of the believers to fear Allah regarding what He has forbidden them and made unlawful for them, namely displaying their faces to non-mahram strangers mentioned in the verse, and a reminder of Allah's witnessing of all things and His knowledge of all things, so that this may serve as an aid to piety.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Explanation of the manners that believers must observe in seeking permission and entering houses for the purpose of a meal or the like.

2- Explanation of the perfection of the Messenger ﷺ in his character, in that he was too shy to say to his guest, "Get out of the house, the meal has ended."

3- Allah, Exalted, described Himself as not being shy of the truth in stating it and commanding it to His servants.

4- The permissibility of addressing a non-mahram woman from behind a screen, curtain or the like.

5- The prohibition of harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that it is a major crime that is not equal to any other.

6- Explanation that a person is not free of evil thoughts when he speaks to a woman and looks at her.

7- The prohibition of marrying the wives of the Messenger after his death, and the prohibition of entertaining a thought of it.

8- Explanation of the mahrams before whom a Muslim woman may uncover her face and speak without a veil.

9- The command to piety and Allah's warning to whoever does not fear Him regarding His prohibitions.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Yuşallūna ʿala al-nabiyy* (يصلون على النبي): God's blessing (ṣalāh) upon the Prophet is His praise and His good pleasure with him. The angels' blessing is supplication and seeking forgiveness for him. The servants' blessing upon him is an honouring and an exalting of his station.

*Ṣallū ʿalayhi wa sallimū taslīman* (صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما): that is, say: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and grant him peace, abundantly."

*Yu'dhūna Allāh wa rasūlahu* (يؤذون الله ورسوله): that is, by means of insult, reviling, slander, or criticism.

*Yu'dhūna al-mu'minīna wa al-mu'mināti bi-ghayri mā ktasabū* (يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا): that is, they accuse them of matters they direct at them as false charges, of which the believers have acquired nothing.

*Faqad ihtamalū buhtānan wa ithman mubīnan* (فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا): that is, they have borne a lie and a manifest sin.

*Yudnīna ʿalayhinna min jalābībihinna* (يدنين عليهن من جلابيبهن): that is, they let down the jilbab over their faces so that nothing of the woman shows except one eye through which she looks at the road when she goes out for a need.

*Dhālika adnā an yuʿrafna* (ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن): that is, this drawing of the edge of the jilbab over the face is closer to (their being recognised).

*Fa-lā yu'dhayna* (فلا يؤذين): that is, they will be known to be free women, so the hypocrites will not molest them.

*Wa kāna Allāh ghafūran raḥīman* (وكان الله غفورا رحيما): that is, He is Forgiving toward whoever repents of his sin, and Merciful to him by accepting his repentance and not punishing him for a sin he has repented of.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When Allah mentioned in the preceding verses what is obligatory upon the believers regarding the honouring and respect of their Prophet, alive and dead, He declared in this verse [56] the nobility of His Prophet, to which no nobility compares, and his exalted rank, to which no rank compares. He informed that He Himself, glory be to Him, sends blessings upon him, that His angels likewise send blessings upon him, and He commanded all believers to send blessings upon him, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.﴾ It is therefore obligatory upon every believing man and woman to send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) at least once in their lifetime, saying: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and grant him peace, abundantly."

The Sunnah has explained several forms of blessing and peace upon the Messenger (ﷺ), the greatest in reward being the *Ṣalāh Ibrāhīmiyyah* (the Ibrahimic blessing, in which the Prophet's blessings are sent as upon Ibrahim). It is obligatory in the final *tashahhud* (the seated testimony recited in prayer, *al-tashahhud al-akhīr*) of every obligatory or voluntary prayer, and it is strongly recommended whenever he (ﷺ) is mentioned and in other occasions. This is what the first verse [56] indicates.

As for the second verse [57], Allah informed His servants that those who harm Allah by lying about Him, or by belittling Him through ascribing incapacity to Him, or attributing to Him a son or a partner, and what is similar to that, such as the depiction of living beings, since creation belongs exclusively to Allah, there being no creator but Him, so imitating Him in creation is not permitted; and those who harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by reviling, insulting, belittling, or attacking him, or his family, his community, his Sunnah, or his religion, these are cursed by Allah in this world and the Hereafter, that is, expelled from His mercy. And He has prepared for them, that is, readied and made present for them, a humiliating punishment which they will taste after their death and on the Day of their resurrection. This is what the third verse [58] indicates.

As for the fourth verse [59], the believing women used to go out at night to relieve themselves, since there were no lavatories in the houses, and some foolish hypocrites would accost them with leering and foolish words, intending by their habit the female slaves and not the free women. The believing women were harmed by this and complained to their husbands about what they suffered from the molestation of some hypocrites. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their jilbābs over themselves.﴾ The *jilbāb* is a wrap or cloak worn over the long, full garment. That is, command them to let down the edge of the wrap over the face until only one eye remains visible through which they can see the way. By this they will be known to be chaste free women, and those hypocrites and fools, upon them be the curse of Allah, will not harm them by molesting them.

As for His saying, ﴿And Allah has always been Forgiving and Merciful﴾, He informed His servants that He, exalted is He, has been and remains Forgiving toward whoever of His servants repents, and Merciful to him, so He does not punish him after his repentance.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation of the nobility of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and the obligation of sending blessings and peace upon him in the final tashahhud of the prayer.

2. Explanation of what befalls whoever harms Allah and His Messenger: wrath and punishment.

3. Explanation of the burden borne by whoever harms believing men and women by speech, attributing to them what they did not say or did not do, or harming them physically by striking the body, taking property, or violating honour.

4. The obligation for a believing woman to cover her face when she goes out for her need, except for an opening through which she can see the way. Today, with the availability of thin fabrics, there is no need to show an eye, since she can let down a cloth over her face, which conceals her face while she sees the road clearly, and praise be to Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 60–62:

Explanation of the words:

﴿La-in lam yantahi al-munafiqun﴾: that is, they do not desist from their hypocrisy (nifaq), which is showing faith while concealing disbelief.

﴿Wa-alladhina fi qulubihim maradh﴾: that is, the sickness of desire for immorality and the lust for fornication.

﴿Wa-al-murjifuna fi al-madinah﴾: that is, those who bring false reports in order to stir up and unsettle souls, such as their saying: "The enemy is close to Madinah," or "such-and-such detachment has been killed," and the like.

﴿Lanughriyannaka bihim﴾: that is, We will give you power over them and We will incite you against them.

﴿Thumma la yujawirunaka fiha illa qalilan﴾: that is, in Madinah, except for a few days, after which they will leave it or be destroyed.

﴿Mal'unina﴾: that is, banished from mercy.

﴿Aynama thuqifu akhidhu﴾: wherever they are found, they will be seized as captives and slain with slaughter.

﴿Sunnata Allahi fi alladhina khalaw min qabl﴾: that is, God has established this sunnah (way/practice) among the past nations: wherever the hypocrites and the rumour-mongers are found, they will be seized and slain with slaughter.

﴿Wa-lan tajida li-sunnati Allahi tabdilan﴾: that is, from Him, the Exalted, since it is not a set of rulings subject to alteration or change, but rather the secret and wisdom of legislation.

Meaning of the verses:

It has already been mentioned that some women complained of what they suffered from the harassment of the hypocrites when they went out at night to relieve themselves, and that God commanded the believing women to draw their outer garments close around them, the reason being that they would be recognised as free women and not be molested by the hypocrites. This was a necessary preventive measure. Then the Almighty swore with His words ﴿Surely if the hypocrites do not desist﴾, meaning: by My might and majesty, if these hypocrites do not desist from their hypocrisy and their provocative deeds, and those in whose hearts is a sickness, the sickness of desire and love of immorality, and the rumour-mongers who spread alarming falsehoods, that is, falsehoods that stir souls, such as their saying: "The enemy is advancing upon Madinah," or "such-and-such detachment has been defeated or most of its members killed"—if these do not desist, then We will incite you against them and then give you power over them. Then they will not dwell beside you in it (Madinah) except for a little while, then they will be expelled from it or destroyed, cursed, that is, expelled and cast out from the divine mercy that reaches the people of the Prophet's city. And then, wherever they are found and come into your power, they will be seized, that is, taken as captives, and slain with slaughter, until none of them remains.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 33, verses 63–68:

Explanation of the words:

"يسألك الناس عن الساعة" (They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour): that is, the Jews of Madina, just as the people of Makka asked. The Jews asked to test him, and the polytheists asked in denial of it and in haste for it.

"قل إنما علمها عند الله" (Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah): that is, answer the questioners by saying: its knowledge is only with my Lord, exclusively; none other than Him knows it.

"وما يدريك" (And what would make you know?): that is, no one can inform you, O Messenger, about it, since its knowledge belongs to Allah alone.

"لعل الساعة تكون قريبا" (Perhaps the Hour is near): that is, what would make you aware that the Hour may be near at hand?

"وأعد لهم سعيرا" (And has prepared for them a blaze): that is, a fire kindled and blazing.

"خالدين فيها" (Abiding therein): that is, their abiding is destined, since abiding occurs after their entry into it.

"تقلب وجوههم في النار" (Their faces will be turned over in the Fire): that is, they will be turned from one side to another, like meat being turned over while being roasted in the fire.

"يا ليتنا أطعنا الله" (Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah): that is, they wish, by their words, that they had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger.

"وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا سادتنا" (And they will say: Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders): this is the saying of the followers, complaining to Allah about their leaders and chiefs.

"فأضلونا السبيلا" (And they led us astray from the way): that is, the path of guidance that leads to the pleasure of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through obedience to Him.

"آتهم ضعفين من العذاب" (Give them double the punishment): that is, make their punishment double our punishment, because they led us astray.

"والعنهم لعنا كبيرا" (And curse them with a great curse): that is, humiliate them with repeated disgrace in the punishment of Hell.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, "يسألك الناس عن الساعة" (They ask you about the Hour), mean: about the appointed time of its coming. The questioners were polytheists and People of the Book. The polytheists asked about it as a way of deeming it far off, so their question was one of mockery, while the Jews asked to test the Messenger ﷺ. So He commanded him to answer the questioners with a single answer, which is "إنما علمها عند الله" (its knowledge is only with Allah), meaning that its knowledge is confined to Allah the Exalted, for Allah has concealed its matter from the angels, from those brought near among them, and likewise from the prophets and messengers among them, let alone from others. So none knows the time of its coming except Him, glorified and exalted. His saying, "وما يدريك" (And what would make you know?), means: no one can inform you of it, O Messenger. His saying, "لعل الساعة تكون قريبا" (Perhaps the Hour is near), means: what would make you aware, O our Messenger, that the Hour may be near at hand? And so He said: "اقترب للناس حسابهم" (Their reckoning has drawn near for the people) [al-Anbiya: 1], and He said: "اقتربت الساعة" (The Hour has drawn near) [al-Qamar: 1]. So He informed of its nearness but did not inform of its time, for lofty wisdoms, among them the continuation of life as it is until the last hour.

His saying, "إن الله لعن الكافرين وأعد لهم سعيرا" (Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze), refers to those who denied the Hour, rejected your message, and denied your prophethood. He cursed them, expelling them from His mercy, and prepared for them a blazing fire in Hell, abiding therein; when they enter it, they will never leave it. "لا يجدون وليا" (They will find no protector) means: one who would take charge of them and repel the punishment from them, "ولا نصيرا" (nor a helper) means: one who would help them and rescue them from their ordeal in Hell. His saying, "يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار" (The Day their faces are turned over in the Fire), means they are turned from one side to another, as meat is turned over when roasted. At that they will say, "يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسول" (Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger), regretting, wishing that they had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger in the world and had not disobeyed Allah and the Messenger. His saying, "وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا" (And they will say: Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders), is a complaint and an excuse from them, but how could their complaint be accepted or their excuse benefit them?

"أطعناهم فيما كانوا يأمروننا به من الكفر والشرك وفعل الشر" (We obeyed them in what they commanded us of disbelief, polytheism, and doing evil), "فأضلونا السبيلا" (and they led us astray from the way), that is, the path of guidance, so we lived misguided and died disbelievers, and were gathered with the criminals. "ربنا" (Our Lord), that is, O our Lord, "آتهم ضعفين من العذاب" (give them double the punishment), that is, multiply, O our Lord, for our leaders and elders who led us astray the punishment; make their punishment double our punishment, "والعنهم" (and curse them), that is, humiliate them in the punishment with a great humiliation that continues upon them always and forever.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that the knowledge of the Hour is exclusively with Allah, so no other knows the time of its coming.

2- Clarification that the Hour is near at hand, and there is no contradiction between its nearness and not knowing when it will occur.

3- Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense by mentioning the states of the disbelievers therein.

4- Clarification that obeying leaders and elders in disobedience to Allah and His Messenger returns with ruin upon those who do it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 33, verses 69–73:

Explanation of the words:

"O you who have believed": that is, O you who have affirmed belief in Allah and His Messenger, and in the meeting with Allah and in what the Messenger of Allah brought.

"Do not be like those who harmed Moses": that is, do not be with your Prophet as the Children of Israel were with Moses, when they harmed him by saying that nothing prevented him from bathing with them except that he had a hernia (ādar).

"So Allah cleared him of what they said": that is, He showed them that he had no adara, which is the swelling of one of the two testicles.

"And he was honourable before Allah": that is, he had great standing with Allah, so his request is never disappointed and his demand is never refused.

"And speak words of appropriate justice": that is, true and correct speech.

"He will amend for you your deeds": that is, both your religious and worldly deeds, for success in deeds and attainment of their fruits depends on truthfulness and conformity with the Sharia.

"Then he has certainly attained a great attainment": that is, he has reached the sought-after goal, which is deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise.

"Indeed, We offered the trust": that is, what man was entrusted with of all the legal obligations, and what one person entrusts to another, whether money, speech, honour or action, to keep.

"So they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it": that is, they refused to undertake it and feared the consequence of neglecting it.

"But man bore it": that is, Adam and his offspring.

"Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant": that is, because he was dhalūm (greatly wronging of himself) and jahūl (ignorant of the consequences).

"That Allah may punish the hypocrites": that is, and man bore it by decree and destiny, so that Allah, exalted is He, may bring about upon it the punishment of hypocrite men and women, and of polytheist men and women, and that He may accept the repentance of believing men and women, forgiving them and showing them mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.

Explanation of the meanings of the verses:

The statement of the Exalted, "O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses": Allah calls the believers of this nation, forbidding them to harm their Prophet even with the least harm, and that they should not be like the Children of Israel who harmed Moses on many occasions. Among these is what the Prophet ﷺ related about him in a narration from Muslim, that the Children of Israel used to bathe naked, each looking at the others, while Moses bathed alone. So they said: "Nothing prevents him from bathing with us except that he has a hernia." One day he went to bathe, placed his garment on a rock and began to wash, but the rock fled with his garment, so Moses ran after it until he stopped with it before a group of the Children of Israel. They saw that he had neither a hernia nor leprosy as they had claimed. This is the meaning of "So Allah cleared him of what they said," and "he was honourable before Allah," that is, he had great standing.

Among the harms the Messenger of Allah ﷺ suffered was the accusation against his wife of immorality by the people of the slander, and the words of someone who said to him, when he had divided some wealth: "This division was not intended for the sake of Allah's countenance." And the words of someone who said: "Be just with us, O Messenger of Allah!" He said to him: "Woe to you! If I am not just, who will be just?" And he used to say: "May Allah have mercy on Moses; he was harmed with more than this and was patient!"

This is what the first verse [69] indicates. As for the second verse [70], the Exalted called His believing servants, whom He had forbidden to harm their Prophet, and not to be in that like the people of Moses son of Imran, calling them to two commands. The first is to be mindful of Him, Mighty and Majestic, when He said: "O you who have believed," that is, who affirm Allah and His Messenger.

"Fear Allah": that is, fear His punishment, so fulfil His obligations and avoid His prohibitions. The second is to adhere to true, correct and appropriate speech. He linked the two commands to the amendment of their deeds and the forgiveness of their sins, since speaking the truth and holding to truthfulness make words and deeds fruitful and beneficial, bringing forth purification of the soul and purity of the spirit. Then He informed them, giving glad tidings, saying: "And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger" in command and prohibition, "has certainly attained a great attainment," which is the happiness of both abodes: deliverance from every fear and attaining every desired beloved thing, among which is deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise. This is what the Exalted's statement contains: "O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice; He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment."

The statement of the Exalted: "Indeed, We offered the trust." He, exalted, informs, admonishing and warning, saying: "Indeed, We offered the trust," which encompasses all the legal obligations and everything a person is entrusted with, of something he keeps for the one who entrusted it to him until he returns it to him. The trust was offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains after Allah had given them intellect and speech, so they understood the address and returned the answer. They refused to bear it with its reward and feared its consequence. It was offered to man, Adam, and he bore it with its consequences of reward and punishment, because he was dhalūm to himself, bringing himself to evil ends, and jahūl of the outcomes of affairs. This is what the fourth verse [72] indicates, which is the statement of the Exalted: "Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant."

The statement of the Exalted: "That Allah may punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists, men and women": that is, by the consequence of hypocrisy and polytheism. "And that Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women": that is, the offering of the trust was completed and Adam accepted it, so that the matter would result in some individuals of mankind disbelieving and being punished for their disbelief, which resulted from neglecting the trust, and others believing, who fall short in some shortcomings but repent, and Allah accepts their repentance, forgives them and admits them to Paradise. "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful." Among the effects of this is that Allah accepted the repentance of the believing men and women, forgave them and showed them mercy by admitting them to Paradise. So glory be to Allah, the Administrator, the Wise.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The obligation of being mindful of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden.

2. Righteous deeds bear fruit for their doers in the purification of the soul, and the goodness of life depends on adhering to truthfulness in speech and action, which is the appropriate speech that excludes lying and deviation in word and deed.

3. Obeying Allah and His Messenger is the path to success and prosperity in both abodes.

4. The obligation to preserve and fulfil trusts, and no one is free of trust.

5. The description of man with injustice, ignorance, disbelief, humiliation and weakness in other verses requires seeking a remedy for these qualities. Its remedy is explained in Surah al-Ma'arij in His statement: "except those who pray" [al-Ma'arij: 22] up to His statement: "and those who are constant in their prayer" [al-Ma'arij: 34].

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 33, verses 69–73:

Explanation of the words:

"O you who have believed": that is, O you who have affirmed belief in Allah and His Messenger, and in the meeting with Allah and in what the Messenger of Allah brought.

"Do not be like those who harmed Moses": that is, do not be with your Prophet as the Children of Israel were with Moses, when they harmed him by saying that nothing prevented him from bathing with them except that he had a hernia (ādar).

"So Allah cleared him of what they said": that is, He showed them that he had no adara, which is the swelling of one of the two testicles.

"And he was honourable before Allah": that is, he had great standing with Allah, so his request is never disappointed and his demand is never refused.

"And speak words of appropriate justice": that is, true and correct speech.

"He will amend for you your deeds": that is, both your religious and worldly deeds, for success in deeds and attainment of their fruits depends on truthfulness and conformity with the Sharia.

"Then he has certainly attained a great attainment": that is, he has reached the sought-after goal, which is deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise.

"Indeed, We offered the trust": that is, what man was entrusted with of all the legal obligations, and what one person entrusts to another, whether money, speech, honour or action, to keep.

"So they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it": that is, they refused to undertake it and feared the consequence of neglecting it.

"But man bore it": that is, Adam and his offspring.

"Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant": that is, because he was dhalūm (greatly wronging of himself) and jahūl (ignorant of the consequences).
